title.zh: 卷一百九十八 列傳第八十六 楊一清 王瓊 彭澤 毛伯溫 翁萬達
title.en: Volume 198 Biographies 86: Yang Yiqing, Wang Qiong, Peng Ze, Mao Bowen, Weng Wanda
title.raw: 卷一百九十八 列傳第八十六 楊一清 王瓊 彭澤 毛伯溫 翁萬達 Volume 198 Biographies 86: Yang Yiqing, Wang Qiong, Peng Ze, Mao Bowen, Weng Wanda

sentences.zh: 楊一清王瓊彭澤毛伯溫

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing, Wang Qiong, Peng Ze, Mao Bowen
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing, Wang Qiong, Peng Ze, and Mao Bowen

sentences.zh: （汪文盛鮑象賢）〉

translations.literal: (Wang Wensheng, Bao Xiangxian)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Wang Wensheng and Bao Xiangxian)〉

sentences.zh: 翁萬達

translations.literal: Weng Wanda
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda

sentences.zh: 楊一清，字應寧，其先雲南安寧人。

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing, style name Yingning, his ancestors were people of Anning in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing, courtesy name Yingning, came from a family originally of Anning in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 父景，以化州同知致仕，攜之居巴陵。

translations.literal: His father Jing, having retired as sub-prefect of Huazhou, took him to live at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang Jing had retired as vice-prefect of Huazhou and brought him to settle at Baling.

sentences.zh: 少能文，以奇童薦為翰林秀才。

translations.literal: In youth he could write; as a prodigy he was recommended and made a Hanlin student.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he showed literary talent and, recommended as a child prodigy, was enrolled as a Hanlin student.

sentences.zh: 憲宗命內閣擇師教之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong ordered the Grand Secretariat to choose teachers to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong directed the Grand Secretariat to select tutors for him.

sentences.zh: 年十四舉鄉試，登成化八年進士。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he passed the provincial examination and in the eighth year of Chenghua attained jinshi rank.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he passed the provincial examination, and in 1472 he received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 父喪，葬丹徒，遂家焉。

translations.literal: When his father died, he buried him at Dantu and thereupon made his home.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he buried him at Dantu and established his household there.

sentences.zh: 服除，授中書舍人。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed a drafting secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷山西按察僉事，以副使督學陜西。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to be Shanxi surveillance commissioner assistant, and as vice commissioner supervised education in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to assistant surveillance commissioner of Shanxi and, as education intendant, oversaw schools in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 一清貌寢而性警敏，好談經濟大略。

translations.literal: Yiqing's appearance was plain yet his nature alert and keen; he loved to discuss statecraft in broad outline.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing was plain in appearance but quick-witted, and loved to discourse on matters of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 在陜八年，以其暇究邊事甚悉。

translations.literal: During eight years in Shaanxi, in his spare time he studied frontier affairs very thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: During eight years in Shaanxi he used his spare time to master frontier affairs in great detail.

sentences.zh: 入為太常寺少卿，進南京太常寺卿。

translations.literal: He entered service as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was advanced to minister of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and later promoted to minister of the Nanjing court.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年用劉大夏薦，擢都察院左副都御史，督理陜西馬政。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi, on Liu Daxia's recommendation, he was raised to left vice censor-in-chief of the Censorate and supervised Shaanxi horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: In 1502, on Liu Daxia's recommendation, he was promoted to left vice censor-in-chief and placed in charge of Shaanxi's horse administration.

sentences.zh: 西番故饒馬，而仰給中國茶飲以去疾。

translations.literal: The western tribes had always been rich in horses, yet relied on Chinese tea to drink for dispelling illness.
translations.idiomatic: The western tribes had long been abundant in horses but depended on Chinese tea to treat their ailments.

sentences.zh: 太祖著令，以蜀茶易番馬，資軍中用。

translations.literal: The founding emperor established an ordinance to exchange Shu tea for tribal horses to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor had decreed that Sichuan tea be traded for tribal horses to supply the military.

sentences.zh: 久而浸弛，奸人多挾私茶闌出為利，番馬不時至。

translations.literal: Over time it gradually lapsed; many scoundrels smuggled private tea across the border for profit, and tribal horses did not arrive on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: In time the system slackened; unscrupulous men smuggled private tea across the border for profit, and tribal horses ceased to arrive regularly.

sentences.zh: 一清嚴為禁，盡籠茶利於官，以服致諸番，番馬大集。

translations.literal: Yiqing strictly enforced the prohibition, gathering all tea profits under the state, and by winning over the tribes caused tribal horses to assemble in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing enforced the prohibition rigorously, monopolized tea profits for the state, won over the tribes, and tribal horses came in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 會寇大入花馬池，帝命一清巡撫陜西，仍督馬政。

translations.literal: Just then bandits made a major incursion at Huama Chi; the emperor ordered Yiqing to serve as Shaanxi grand coordinator while still supervising horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders launched a major attack on Huama Chi, the emperor appointed Yiqing grand coordinator of Shaanxi while retaining his charge over horse administration.

sentences.zh: 甫受事，寇已退。

translations.literal: He had just taken office when the bandits had already withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely assumed his post when the raiders had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 乃選卒練兵，創平虜、紅古二城以援固原；

translations.literal: Thereupon he selected soldiers and trained troops, and founded the two cities Pinglu and Honggu to support Guyuan;
translations.idiomatic: He then selected troops for training and built the two garrison towns of Pinglu and Honggu to reinforce Guyuan;

sentences.zh: 築垣瀕河以捍靖虜；

translations.literal: he built walls along the riverbank to defend Jinglu;
translations.idiomatic: constructed riverfront ramparts to shield Jinglu;

sentences.zh: 劾罷貪庸總兵武安侯鄭宏；

translations.literal: he impeached and removed the greedy and incompetent regional commander, Marquis Wu'an Zheng Hong;
translations.idiomatic: impeached and dismissed the corrupt and inept regional commander, Marquis of Wu'an Zheng Hong;

sentences.zh: 裁鎮守中官冗費，軍紀肅然。

translations.literal: he cut redundant expenses of the eunuch defenders, and military discipline became strict.
translations.idiomatic: and trimmed the wasteful spending of the eunuch garrison commissioners, bringing military discipline to order.

sentences.zh: 武宗初立，寇數萬騎抵固原，總兵曹雄軍隔絕不相聞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong had just ascended, bandits with tens of thousands of horsemen reached Guyuan; regional commander Cao Xiong's army was cut off and could not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after Emperor Wuzong's accession, raiders with tens of thousands of horsemen reached Guyuan, while Regional Commander Cao Xiong's forces were cut off and out of contact.

sentences.zh: 一清帥輕騎自平涼晝夜行，抵雄軍，為之節度，多張疑兵脅寇，寇移犯隆德。

translations.literal: Yiqing led light cavalry from Pingliang, traveling day and night, reached Xiong's army, directed it, and deployed many decoys to threaten the bandits; the bandits shifted to attack Longde.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing led light cavalry from Pingliang in a forced march, joined Xiong's army, took command, and deployed numerous decoys to intimidate the raiders, who then turned toward Longde.

sentences.zh: 一清夜發火炮，響應山谷間。

translations.literal: Yiqing fired cannon at night, and the echoes resounded through the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yiqing fired cannon, and the echoes rolled through the valleys.

sentences.zh: 寇疑大兵至，遁出塞。

translations.literal: The bandits suspected a great army had arrived and fled beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders, suspecting a large army had arrived, fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 一清以延綏、寧夏、甘肅有警不相援，患無所統攝，請遣大臣兼領之。

translations.literal: Yiqing, because Yan-sui, Ningxia, and Gansu had alarms yet did not aid one another, worried that there was no unified command, and requested that a senior minister be sent to oversee them jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing observed that when Yan-sui, Ningxia, and Gansu faced alarms they failed to support one another for lack of unified command, and petitioned that a senior minister be sent to oversee all three.

sentences.zh: 大夏請即命一清總制三鎮軍務。

translations.literal: Daxia requested that Yiqing immediately be ordered to take overall command of the three garrisons' military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daxia recommended that Yiqing be appointed at once to take overall command of military affairs in all three regions.

sentences.zh: 尋進右都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 一清遂建議修邊，其略曰：

translations.literal: Yiqing thereupon proposed repairing the frontier; the gist said:
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing then submitted a proposal for frontier defense, which in summary stated:

sentences.zh: 陜西各邊，延綏據險，寧夏、甘肅扼河山，惟花馬池至靈州地寬延，城堡復疏。

translations.literal: On the various frontiers of Shaanxi, Yan-sui held strategic terrain, Ningxia and Gansu straddled river and mountain, but only from Huama Chi to Lingzhou was the ground broad and extended, and fortresses were again sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Among Shaanxi's frontiers, Yan-sui held defensible terrain and Ningxia and Gansu guarded the rivers and mountains, but from Huama Chi to Lingzhou the land was open and extended, and fortifications were thin.

sentences.zh: 寇毀墻入，則固原、慶陽、平涼、鞏昌皆受患。

translations.literal: If bandits broke the wall and entered, then Guyuan, Qingyang, Pingliang, and Gongchang would all suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Once raiders breached the walls, Guyuan, Qingyang, Pingliang, and Gongchang would all be exposed to attack.

sentences.zh: 成化初，寧夏巡撫徐廷璋築邊墻綿亙二百餘里。

translations.literal: In early Chenghua, Ningxia grand coordinator Xu Tingzhang built a frontier wall extending over two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chenghua reign, Ningxia Grand Coordinator Xu Tingzhang built a frontier wall more than two hundred li long.

sentences.zh: 在延綏者，余子俊修之甚固。

translations.literal: That in Yan-sui was repaired very solidly by Yu Zijun.
translations.idiomatic: The wall in Yan-sui was repaired very solidly by Yu Zijun.

sentences.zh: 由是，寇不入套二十余年。

translations.literal: Because of this, for more than twenty years bandits did not enter the Ordos.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, raiders did not enter the Ordos for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 後邊備疏，墻塹日夷。

translations.literal: Later frontier defense grew lax, and walls and ditches daily crumbled.
translations.idiomatic: Later frontier defenses grew lax, and walls and ditches fell into ruin day by day.

sentences.zh: 弘治末至今，寇連歲侵略。

translations.literal: From late Hongzhi to the present, bandits have invaded year after year.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Hongzhi period to the present, raiders have attacked year after year.

sentences.zh: 都御史史琳請於花馬池、韋州設營衛，總制尚書秦纮僅修四五小堡及靖虜至環慶治塹七百里，謂可無患。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Shi Lin requested establishing camps and guards at Huama Chi and Weizhou; overall commander Minister Qin Hong only repaired four or five small forts and dredged ditches seven hundred li from Jinglu to Huanqing, saying there would be no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Shi Lin had proposed establishing garrisons at Huama Chi and Weizhou; Overall Commander Qin Hong had only repaired four or five small forts and cleared ditches for seven hundred li from Jinglu to Huanqing, claiming this would suffice.

sentences.zh: 不一二年，寇復深入。

translations.literal: In no more than one or two years, bandits again penetrated deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year or two the raiders penetrated deep again.

sentences.zh: 是纮所修不足捍敵。

translations.literal: Thus what Hong repaired was insufficient to repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hong's repairs had proved inadequate to hold the enemy at bay.

sentences.zh: 臣久官陜西，頗諳形勢。

translations.literal: Your servant has long served in Shaanxi and is fairly well acquainted with the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has long served in Shaanxi and is well acquainted with the terrain.

sentences.zh: 寇動稱數萬，往來倏忽。

translations.literal: Bandits routinely claim tens of thousands and come and go in a flash.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders routinely claim tens of thousands of men and move with lightning speed.

sentences.zh: 未至，征兵多擾費；

translations.literal: Before they arrive, mobilizing troops mostly wastes funds in disruption;
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrive, mobilizing troops mostly wastes money in futile disruption;

sentences.zh: 既至，召援輒後時。

translations.literal: once they arrive, calling for reinforcements is always too late.
translations.idiomatic: once they strike, calling for reinforcements is always too late.

sentences.zh: 欲戰，則彼不來；

translations.literal: If we wish to fight, they do not come;
translations.idiomatic: If we seek battle, they will not engage;

sentences.zh: 持久，則我師坐老。

translations.literal: if we hold out long, our army sits and grows old.
translations.idiomatic: if we wait them out, our troops are worn down in idleness.

sentences.zh: 臣以為防邊之策，大要有四：修浚墻塹，以固邊防；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that strategies for defending the frontier have four main points: repair and dredge walls and ditches to strengthen frontier defense;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes frontier defense rests on four main measures: repair walls and ditches to strengthen the border;

sentences.zh: 增設衛所，以壯邊兵；

translations.literal: add guards and battalions to augment frontier troops;
translations.idiomatic: establish new garrisons to strengthen frontier forces;

sentences.zh: 經理靈、夏，以安內附；

translations.literal: administer Ling and Xia to settle those who have submitted within;
translations.idiomatic: administer Lingzhou and Ningxia to secure those tribes who have submitted;

sentences.zh: 整飭韋州，以遏外侵。

translations.literal: put Weizhou in order to check external invasion.
translations.idiomatic: and put Weizhou in order to block external incursions.

sentences.zh: 今河套即周朔方，漢定襄，赫連勃勃統萬城也。

translations.literal: Present-day Ordos is Zhou's Shuofang, Han's Dingxiang, and Helian Bobo's Tongwan city.
translations.idiomatic: The Ordos of today was the Zhou domain of Shuofang, the Han commandery of Dingxiang, and the site of Helian Bobo's capital at Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 唐張仁願築三受降城，置烽堠千八百所，突厥不敢逾山牧馬。

translations.literal: In Tang, Zhang Renyuan built the three cities for receiving surrender, set up eighteen hundred beacon towers, and the Turks dared not cross the mountains to pasture horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times Zhang Renyuan built the three surrender cities and established eighteen hundred beacon towers, and the Turks dared not cross the mountains to pasture their herds.

sentences.zh: 古之舉大事者，未嘗不勞於先，逸於後。

translations.literal: Those who undertook great affairs in antiquity never failed to toil first and rest afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Those who undertook great enterprises in antiquity always labored first and enjoyed ease afterward.

sentences.zh: 夫受降據三面險，當千里之蔽。

translations.literal: The surrender cities held danger on three sides and stood as a shield for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The surrender cities held strategic terrain on three sides and shielded a thousand li of frontier.

sentences.zh: 國初舍受降而衛東勝，已失一面之險。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, abandoning the surrender cities to guard Dongsheng already lost one side's strategic advantage.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding, abandoning the surrender cities to guard Dongsheng already sacrificed one flank's strategic advantage.

sentences.zh: 其後又輟東勝以就延綏，則以一面而遮千餘里之沖，遂使河套沃壤為寇巢穴。

translations.literal: Later Dongsheng was also abandoned in favor of Yan-sui, so that with one flank blocking a thrust of more than a thousand li, the fertile soil of the Ordos became the bandits' nest.
translations.idiomatic: Later Dongsheng was abandoned in turn for Yan-sui, leaving a single flank to block an attack front of more than a thousand li and turning the fertile Ordos into the raiders' stronghold.

sentences.zh: 深山大河，勢乃在彼，而寧夏外險反南備河。

translations.literal: Deep mountains and great rivers—the strategic advantage lies with them—while Ningxia's outer defenses instead face south to guard the river.
translations.idiomatic: The deep mountains and great rivers give the enemy the advantage, while Ningxia's outer defenses face south to guard the river instead.

sentences.zh: 此邊患所以相尋而不可解也。

translations.literal: This is why frontier troubles follow one upon another and cannot be resolved.
translations.idiomatic: This is why frontier troubles follow one upon another without end.

sentences.zh: 誠宜復守東勝，因河為固，東接大同，西屬寧夏，使河套方千里之地，歸我耕牧，屯田數百萬畝，省內地轉輸，策之上也。

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to restore the guard at Dongsheng, take the river as a bulwark, connect east to Datong and west to Ningxia, and cause the Ordos' roughly thousand-li square to return to our farming and herding, with garrison fields of several million mu, saving interior transport—this is the superior policy.
translations.idiomatic: We should truly restore the garrison at Dongsheng, use the river as our bulwark, link east to Datong and west to Ningxia, and recover the thousand-li square of the Ordos for farming and grazing, with garrison colonies of millions of mu and savings on grain transport from the interior—this would be the best policy.

sentences.zh: 如或不能，及今增築防邊，敵來有以待之，猶愈無策。

translations.literal: If that cannot be done, then at least now increase frontier fortifications so that when the enemy comes there is something to meet them—still better than no plan.
translations.idiomatic: If that cannot be done, we should at least strengthen frontier defenses now so that when the enemy comes we are prepared—still better than having no plan at all.

sentences.zh: 因條具便宜：延綏安邊營石澇池至橫城三百里，宜設墩臺九百座，暖譙九百間，守軍四千五百人；

translations.literal: He thereupon itemized expedients: from Shilao Chi to Hengcheng along the three hundred li of Yan-sui's Anbian camp, there should be nine hundred beacon platforms, nine hundred warmed watch towers, and four thousand five hundred garrison troops;
translations.idiomatic: He then itemized specific measures: along the three hundred li from Shilao Chi to Hengcheng in Yan-sui's Anbian sector, nine hundred beacon platforms, nine hundred heated watch towers, and four thousand five hundred garrison troops should be established;

sentences.zh: 石澇池至定邊營百六十三里，平衍宜墻者百三十一里，險崖峻阜可鏟削者三十二里，宜為墩臺，連接寧夏東路；

translations.literal: from Shilao Chi to Dingbian camp one hundred sixty-three li—of level ground fit for walls one hundred thirty-one li, of perilous cliffs and steep heights that can be cut and shaved thirty-two li—beacon platforms should be made to link with Ningxia's eastern route;
translations.idiomatic: along the one hundred sixty-three li from Shilao Chi to Dingbian camp, walls should be built for one hundred thirty-one li of level ground and beacon platforms cut into thirty-two li of steep cliffs, linking with Ningxia's eastern route;

sentences.zh: 花馬池無險，敵至仰客兵，宜置衛；

translations.literal: Huama Chi has no natural barrier; when the enemy arrives it relies on guest troops—a guard should be established;
translations.idiomatic: Huama Chi lacks natural defenses and must rely on auxiliary troops when the enemy strikes—a garrison should be established there;

sentences.zh: 興武營守禦所兵不足，宜召募；

translations.literal: Xingwu camp's defense battalion has insufficient troops and should recruit;
translations.idiomatic: the Xingwu defense battalion lacks sufficient troops and should recruit more;

sentences.zh: 自環慶以西至寧州，宜增兵備一人；

translations.literal: from Huanqing west to Ningzhou, one additional military intendant should be added;
translations.idiomatic: from Huanqing west to Ningzhou, an additional military intendant should be appointed;

sentences.zh: 橫城以北，黃河南岸有墩三十六，宜修復。

translations.literal: north of Hengcheng on the south bank of the Yellow River there are thirty-six beacons that should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: north of Hengcheng, thirty-six beacons on the south bank of the Yellow River should be restored.

sentences.zh: 帝可其議。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 大發帑金數十萬，使一清築墻。

translations.literal: He greatly disbursed several hundred thousand taels from the treasury to have Yiqing build the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred thousand taels were released from the treasury for Yiqing to build the wall.

sentences.zh: 而劉瑾憾一清不附己，一清遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: But Liu Jin resented that Yiqing would not attach himself to him, and Yiqing thereupon cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Jin resented Yiqing's refusal to join his faction, and Yiqing cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 其成者，在要害間僅四十里。

translations.literal: Of what was completed, only forty li in critical places.
translations.idiomatic: Of what was actually completed, only forty li in the most critical sectors.

sentences.zh: 瑾誣一清冒破邊費，逮下錦衣獄。

translations.literal: Jin falsely accused Yiqing of falsely claiming and squandering frontier funds and had him arrested and sent to the Embroidered Uniform prison.
translations.idiomatic: Jin falsely accused Yiqing of embezzling frontier funds and had him imprisoned in the Embroidered Uniform Guard jail.

sentences.zh: 大學士李東陽、王鏊力救得解。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries Li Dongyang and Wang Ao strenuously rescued him and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Li Dongyang and Wang Ao intervened strenuously and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 仍致仕歸，先後罰米六百石。

translations.literal: He still retired and returned home, and in all was fined six hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He still retired home and was fined six hundred piculs of grain in all.

sentences.zh: 安化王寘鐇反。

translations.literal: Prince of Anhua Zhu Zhifan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Anhua, Zhu Zhifan, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 詔起一清總制軍務，與總兵官神英西討，中官張永監其軍。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Yiqing to take overall command of military affairs; with regional commander Shen Ying he marched west to punish them, and eunuch Zhang Yong supervised the army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Yiqing to take overall command; with Regional Commander Shen Ying he marched west to suppress the rebellion, while the eunuch Zhang Yong supervised the army.

sentences.zh: 未至，一清故部將仇鉞已捕執之。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Yiqing's former subordinate general Qiu Yi had already captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Yiqing's former subordinate Qiu Yi had already captured the prince.

sentences.zh: 一清馳至鎮，宣布德意。

translations.literal: Yiqing galloped to the garrison and proclaimed the emperor's gracious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing rode swiftly to the garrison and proclaimed the emperor's benevolent intentions.

sentences.zh: 張永旋亦至，一清與結納，相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong soon also arrived; Yiqing formed a bond with him and they got on very well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong soon arrived as well; Yiqing befriended him and they became quite close.

sentences.zh: 知永與瑾有隙，乘間扼腕言曰：「賴公力定反側。

translations.literal: Knowing that Yong and Jin were at odds, he seized an opportunity, clenching his wrist, and said: 'Thanks to your power the rebellion was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Yong and Jin were at odds, he seized a moment, gripped his arm, and said, "Thanks to your efforts the rebellion has been put down.

sentences.zh: 然此易除也，如國家內患何。

translations.literal: Yet this was easy to remove; what of the state's internal affliction?'
translations.idiomatic: But that was easy to remove. What of the state's internal affliction?"

sentences.zh: 」永曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: Yong said: 'What do you mean?'
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 」一清遂促席畫掌作「瑾」字。

translations.literal: Yiqing then drew close and traced the character 'Jin' on his palm.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing drew closer and traced the character for Jin on his palm.

sentences.zh: 永難之曰：「是家晨夕上前，枝附根據，耳目廣矣。

translations.literal: Yong demurred: 'That family is morning and evening before the throne, with branches attached and roots planted—its eyes and ears are wide indeed.'
translations.idiomatic: Yong hesitated. "That family is at the emperor's side morning and night, with branches and roots everywhere, and eyes and ears throughout the court."

sentences.zh: 」一清慷慨曰：「公亦上信臣，討賊不付他人而付公，意可知。

translations.literal: Yiqing said fervently: 'You too are trusted by the sovereign; to suppress bandits he did not entrust others but entrusted you—the intent is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing said fervently, "The emperor trusts you as well. He did not entrust the campaign to anyone else but to you—his intent is clear.

sentences.zh: 今功成奏捷，請間論軍事，因發瑾奸，極陳海內愁怨，懼變起心腹。

translations.literal: Now with merit achieved and victory reported, request a private audience to discuss military affairs, and thereby expose Jin's wickedness, fully set forth the realm's grief and resentment, and fear that trouble will arise at the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have won, report your victory and request a private audience on military affairs. There expose Jin's crimes, lay bare the realm's grievances, and warn that trouble may erupt at the very center of power.

sentences.zh: 上英武，必聽公誅瑾。

translations.literal: The sovereign is martial and resolute; he will surely heed you and execute Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is resolute; he will surely heed you and execute Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，公益柄用，悉矯前弊，收天下心。

translations.literal: Once Jin is executed, you will further wield power, fully correct previous abuses, and win all hearts under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin is dead, you will wield even greater power, correct all past abuses, and win the hearts of the empire.

sentences.zh: 呂強、張承業暨公，千載三人耳。

translations.literal: Lü Qiang, Zhang Chengye, and you—only three men in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Qiang, Zhang Chengye, and you—only three such men in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 」永曰：「脫不濟，奈何？

translations.literal: Yong said: 'If it fails, what then?'
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "But if it fails, what then?"

sentences.zh: 」一清曰：「言出於公必濟。

translations.literal: Yiqing said: 'Words coming from you will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing said, "Words from you will surely succeed.

sentences.zh: 萬一不信，公頓首據地泣，請死上前，剖心以明不妄，上必為公動。

translations.literal: In the one case of disbelief, you should bow your head, beat the ground, and weep, begging death before the throne and laying open your heart to show you do not speak falsely—the sovereign will surely be moved for you.
translations.idiomatic: If he does not believe you, bow your head, beat the ground, and weep before him; beg for death and lay bare your heart to prove you speak truth—the emperor will surely be moved.

sentences.zh: 茍得請，即行事，毋須臾緩。

translations.literal: If you obtain permission, act at once; do not delay for an instant.
translations.idiomatic: Once you have permission, act at once without the slightest delay.

sentences.zh: 」於是永勃然起曰：「嗟乎，老奴何惜余年不以報主哉！

translations.literal: Thereupon Yong rose abruptly and said: 'Alas, why should this old slave begrudge his remaining years and not repay his lord!'
translations.idiomatic: At this Yong rose abruptly and cried, "Alas! Why should this old servant begrudge his remaining years rather than repay his lord!"

sentences.zh: 」竟如一清策誅瑾。

translations.literal: In the end he followed Yiqing's plan and executed Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he followed Yiqing's plan and had Jin executed.

sentences.zh: 永以是德一清，左右之，得召還，拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Yong for this was grateful to Yiqing, supported him at court, and he was recalled and appointed minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was grateful to Yiqing for this, supported him at court, and Yiqing was recalled and appointed minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子少保，賜金幣。

translations.literal: For merit he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and bestowed gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and rewarded with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 尋改吏部。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 一清於時政最通練，而性闊大。

translations.literal: Yiqing was most thoroughly versed in current affairs, yet his nature was broad and magnanimous.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing was the most thoroughly versed in current affairs of his day, yet his temperament was broad and magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 愛樂賢士大夫，與共功名。

translations.literal: He loved and delighted in worthy scholar-officials and shared merit and fame with them.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in worthy scholar-officials and shared glory with them.

sentences.zh: 凡為瑾所構陷者，率見甄錄。

translations.literal: All who had been framed by Jin were in general selected and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: All who had been framed by Liu Jin were in general restored to office.

sentences.zh: 朝有所知，夕即登薦，門生遍天下。

translations.literal: If he knew someone in the morning, by evening he would recommend them; his disciples were everywhere under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If he learned of talent in the morning, he would recommend it by evening; his protégés were found throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 嘗再帥關中，起偏裨至大將封侯者，累累然不絕。

translations.literal: He twice commanded Guanzhong; from junior officers to great generals enfeoffed as marquises, they came forth in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he commanded in the Guanzhong region, and from junior officers to great generals enfeoffed as marquises, he raised them in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 饋謝有所入，緣手即散之。

translations.literal: When gifts and thanks brought income, as soon as it passed through his hands he dispersed it.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever gifts or gratuities came to him he passed on at once.

sentences.zh: 大盜躪中原，一清疏請命將調兵。

translations.literal: Great bandits trampled the central plains; Yiqing memorialized requesting that generals be appointed and troops mobilized.
translations.idiomatic: When great bandit armies ravaged the central plains, Yiqing memorialized asking that generals be appointed and troops mobilized.

sentences.zh: 前後凡數上，皆報可。

translations.literal: In all he submitted several memorials, and all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted several such memorials in succession, and all were approved.

sentences.zh: 盜平，加少保、太子太保，蔭錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was given the additional titles Junior Guardian and Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with hereditary enrollment of one hundred Embroidered Uniform households.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were pacified, he was made Junior Guardian and Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with hereditary enrollment of one hundred Embroidered Uniform Guard households.

sentences.zh: 再推內閣，不用。

translations.literal: He was again recommended for the Grand Secretariat but was not used.
translations.idiomatic: He was again recommended for the Grand Secretariat but was passed over.

sentences.zh: 用尚書靳貴，而進一清少傅、太子太傅。

translations.literal: Minister Jin Gui was used, while Yiqing was advanced to Junior Tutor and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Jin Gui was appointed instead, while Yiqing was promoted to Junior Tutor and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 給事中王昂論選法幣，指一清植私黨，帝為謫昂。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Wang Ang discussed selection-law abuses and accused Yiqing of cultivating a private faction; the emperor demoted Ang on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wang Ang criticized abuses in the selection system and accused Yiqing of building a private faction; the emperor demoted Ang on Yiqing's behalf.

sentences.zh: 一清更申救，優旨報聞。

translations.literal: Yiqing further pleaded for his rescue, and an edict of favor was issued in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing interceded for him again, and the emperor responded with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮災，詔求直言。

translations.literal: When the Qianqing Palace suffered fire, an edict sought forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: When fire struck the Qianqing Palace, the emperor issued an edict calling for forthright counsel.

sentences.zh: 一清上書言視朝太遲，享祀太慢，西內創梵宇，禁中宿邊兵，畿內皇店之害，江南織造之擾。

translations.literal: Yiqing submitted a memorial saying that audiences were too late, sacrifices too slow, Buddhist halls were built in the western inner palace, frontier troops lodged in the forbidden precinct, the harm of imperial shops within the capital region, and the disturbance of Jiangnan weaving commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing memorialized that imperial audiences began too late, sacrifices were performed too slowly, Buddhist temples had been built in the western inner palace, frontier troops were quartered within the forbidden city, imperial shops in the capital region were causing harm, and Jiangnan weaving commissions were causing disruption.

sentences.zh: 因引疾乞歸，帝慰留之。

translations.literal: He thereupon cited illness and begged to return home; the emperor comforted him and kept him.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited illness and asked to retire, but the emperor comforted him and kept him at court.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊廷和憂去，命一清兼武英殿大學士入參機務。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe left on mourning, Yiqing was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall and enter to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe left office to mourn, Yiqing was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall and join in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 張永尋得罪罷，而義子錢寧用事。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong soon fell into disgrace and was dismissed, while the adopted son Qian Ning wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong soon fell from favor and was dismissed, while the emperor's adopted son Qian Ning came to power.

sentences.zh: 寧故善一清，有構之者因蓄怨。

translations.literal: Ning had formerly been on good terms with Yiqing, but those who sowed discord between them thus harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Ning had formerly been on good terms with Yiqing, but those who sowed discord between them bred resentment.

sentences.zh: 會災異，一清自劾，極陳時政，中有「狂言惑聖聽，匹夫搖國是，禁廷雜介胄之夫，京師無藩籬之托」語，譏切近幸，帝弗省。

translations.literal: When calamities and anomalies occurred, Yiqing impeached himself and fully set forth current policy, including the words 'mad words delude the sage's hearing, a common man shakes the state's course, the forbidden court mixes men in armor, and the capital has no hedge of protection'—cutting at the emperor's favorites; the emperor did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: When omens and disasters occurred, Yiqing submitted a self-impeachment laying out current abuses, including the words, "reckless talk deludes the emperor's ear, a common man shakes the course of state, the forbidden court is filled with men in armor, and the capital lacks any protective barrier"—a cutting rebuke of the emperor's favorites, which the emperor did not heed.

sentences.zh: 寧與江彬輩聞之，大怒。

translations.literal: Ning and Jiang Bin and their ilk heard it and were greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Ning and Jiang Bin and their faction heard this and were furious.

sentences.zh: 使優人於帝前為蜚語，刺譏一清。

translations.literal: They had actors before the emperor perform slanderous words mocking Yiqing.
translations.idiomatic: They had actors perform before the emperor with slanderous lines aimed at Yiqing.

sentences.zh: 時有考察罷官者，嗾武學生朱大周訐一清陰事，而以寧為內主。

translations.literal: At the time there was one dismissed in the evaluation of officials; they instigated military student Zhu Dazhou to accuse Yiqing of secret matters, with Ning as the hidden patron.
translations.idiomatic: An official dismissed in the regular evaluation was instigated to set Military Student Zhu Dazhou to accuse Yiqing of secret misconduct, with Ning as the hidden patron behind the attack.

sentences.zh: 給事御史周金、陳軾等交章劾大周妄言，請究主使，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors Zhou Jin, Chen Shi, and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Dazhou for reckless speech and requesting investigation of the instigator; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors Zhou Jin, Chen Shi, and others submitted successive memorials accusing Dazhou of false charges and demanding that the instigator be investigated; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 一清乃力請骸骨歸，賜敕褒諭，給夫廩如制。

translations.literal: Yiqing then strenuously requested to return home on his bones; he was granted an edict of praise and consolation, with carriers and grain allowance according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing then pressed hard to retire, and was granted an edict of praise and consolation, with carriers and grain allowance according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 帝南征，幸一清第，樂飲兩晝夜，賦詩賡和以十數。

translations.literal: When the emperor marched south, he visited Yiqing's residence, feasted and drank for two days and nights, and composed and responded to poems numbering more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign the emperor visited Yiqing's residence, feasted with him for two days and nights, and composed and exchanged more than ten poems.

sentences.zh: 一清從容諷止，帝遂不為江浙行。

translations.literal: Yiqing gently admonished and stopped him, and the emperor thereupon did not proceed to Jiangsu and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing gently dissuaded him, and the emperor abandoned his planned tour of Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 會張璁等力排費宏，御史吉棠因請還一清內閣。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cong and others forcefully drove out Fei Hong, censor Ji Tang thereupon requested that Yiqing be returned to the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong and others forced Fei Hong from office, Censor Ji Tang petitioned to recall Yiqing to the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 給事中章僑、御史侯秩等爭之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Zhang Qiao, censor Hou Zhi, and others disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Qiao, Censor Hou Zhi, and others protested.

sentences.zh: 帝謫秩官，召一清為吏部尚書、武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: The emperor demoted Zhi's office and summoned Yiqing as minister of personnel and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demoted Hou Zhi and summoned Yiqing as minister of personnel and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 既入見，加少師，仍兼太子太傅，非故事也。

translations.literal: After he entered audience, he was given the additional title Junior Preceptor and still held concurrently Tutor of the Heir Apparent—not precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After his audience he was made Junior Preceptor while retaining the concurrent post of Tutor of the Heir Apparent—an unprecedented arrangement.

sentences.zh: 亡何，《獻皇帝實錄》成，加太子太師、謹身殿大學士。

translations.literal: Before long, when the Veritable Record of the Xian Emperor was completed, he was given Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when the Veritable Record of the Xian Emperor was completed, he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall.

sentences.zh: 一清以不預纂修辭，不許。

translations.literal: Yiqing declined on the ground that he had not participated in the compilation; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing declined on the ground that he had not taken part in the compilation, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 王憲奏捷，推功一清，加特進左柱國、華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: When Wang Xian reported victory, merit was attributed to Yiqing; he was given special advancement as Left Pillar of the State and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xian reported victory, credit was given to Yiqing, who was granted special advancement as Left Pillar of the State and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall.

sentences.zh: 費宏已去，一清遂為首輔。

translations.literal: Fei Hong had already departed, and Yiqing thereupon became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: With Fei Hong already gone, Yiqing became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 帝賜銀章二，曰「耆德忠正」，曰「繩愆糾違」，令密封言事。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed two silver seals, reading 'aged in virtue and loyal and upright' and 'correcting faults and rectifying transgressions,' ordering sealed memorials on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed two silver seals inscribed "aged in virtue and loyal and upright" and "correcting faults and rectifying transgressions," authorizing him to submit sealed memorials on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 與張璁論張永前功，起為提督團營。

translations.literal: Discussing Zhang Yong's former merit with Zhang Cong, he was raised to supervise the regimented camps.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Cong argued for Zhang Yong's former merit, Yong was restored to command of the regimented camps.

sentences.zh: 給事中陸粲請增築邊墻，推明一清曩時議，一清因力從臾之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Lu Can requested increasing construction of the frontier wall, elaborating Yiqing's former proposal; Yiqing thereupon strongly urged it on.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Lu Can petitioned to extend the frontier wall, citing Yiqing's earlier proposal, and Yiqing strongly pressed the measure.

sentences.zh: 帝為發帑金，命侍郎王廷相往，然久之亦竟止。

translations.literal: The emperor released treasury funds and ordered vice minister Wang Tingxiang to go, yet after a long while it also ended in cessation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released treasury funds and ordered Vice Minister Wang Tingxiang to oversee the work, but in time the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 《明倫大典》成，加正一品俸。

translations.literal: When the Great Canon of Bright Relations was completed, he was given salary of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Canon of Bright Relations was completed, he was granted salary of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 初，「大禮」議起，一清方家居，見張璁疏，寓書門人喬宇曰：「張生此議，聖人復起，不能易也。

translations.literal: At first, when the 'Great Rites' debate arose, Yiqing was at home and, seeing Zhang Cong's memorial, sent a letter through his disciple Qiao Yu saying: 'Student Zhang's argument—if a sage arose again, he could not change it.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Great Rites controversy, Yiqing was at home. Reading Zhang Cong's memorial, he wrote to his disciple Qiao Yu, "Zhang's argument is such that even if a sage were to rise again, he could not overturn it.

sentences.zh: 」又勸席書早赴召，以定大議。

translations.literal: ' He also urged Xi Shu to hurry to answer the summons and settle the great debate.
translations.idiomatic: " He also urged Xi Shu to hurry to court and settle the great debate.

sentences.zh: 璁等既驟顯，頗引一清。

translations.literal: Cong and the others, having suddenly risen to prominence, drew on Yiqing considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Cong and his allies rose to power, they drew heavily on Yiqing's support.

sentences.zh: 帝亦以一清老臣，恩禮加渥。

translations.literal: The emperor also, because Yiqing was an aged minister, added generous favor and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also treated Yiqing, as a senior minister, with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 免常朝日講侍班，朔望朝參，令晨初始入閣視事。

translations.literal: He was exempted from daily audience, daily lecture attendance, and morning and evening court; he was ordered to enter the Grand Secretariat to handle affairs only from early morning.
translations.idiomatic: He was exempted from daily audiences and lecture attendance, attended court only on the first and fifteenth of the month, and was ordered to enter the Grand Secretariat to conduct business only from early morning.

sentences.zh: 禦書、和章及金幣、牢醴之賜甚渥。

translations.literal: Imperial writings, harmonizing compositions, and gifts of gold, silks, and sacrificial offerings were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial writings, matching poems, and gifts of gold, silks, and sacrificial offerings were lavished upon him.

sentences.zh: 所言邊事、國計，大小無不傾聽。

translations.literal: Whatever he spoke on frontier affairs or national finance, great or small, the emperor listened with full attention.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he said on frontier affairs or state finance, great or small, the emperor listened attentively.

sentences.zh: 璁與桂萼既攻去費宏，意一清必援己。

translations.literal: Cong and Gui E, having already attacked and removed Fei Hong, expected that Yiqing would certainly aid them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E, having driven Fei Hong from office, expected Yiqing to support them.

sentences.zh: 一清顧請召謝遷，心怨之。

translations.literal: Yiqing instead requested that Xie Qian be summoned; they resented this in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing instead petitioned to recall Xie Qian, and they resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 遷未至，璁已入內閣，多所更建。

translations.literal: Before Qian arrived, Cong had already entered the Grand Secretariat and made many changes and innovations.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xie Qian arrived, Zhang Cong had already entered the Grand Secretariat and instituted many changes.

sentences.zh: 一清引故事稍裁抑，其黨積不平。

translations.literal: Yiqing cited precedent to restrain them somewhat, and their faction accumulated resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing cited precedent to restrain them somewhat, and their faction grew increasingly resentful.

sentences.zh: 錦衣聶能遷訐璁，璁欲置之死，一清不可。

translations.literal: Embroidered Uniform Guard Nie Nengqian accused Cong; Cong wished to have him put to death, but Yiqing would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Embroidered Uniform Guard Nie Nengqian accused Zhang Cong, who wished to have him executed; Yiqing would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 璁怒，上疏陰詆一清，又嗾黃綰排之甚力。

translations.literal: Cong was enraged, submitted a memorial secretly slandering Yiqing, and also instigated Huang Guan to attack him very forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong was enraged, submitted a secret memorial slandering Yiqing, and also instigated Huang Guan to attack him fiercely.

sentences.zh: 一清疏辨，言璁以能遷故排己，且傍及璁他語。

translations.literal: Yiqing memorialized in defense, saying Cong attacked him because of Nengqian, and also touched on Cong's other words.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing memorialized in defense, saying Zhang Cong attacked him because of the Nie Nengqian affair and also alluding to Cong's other misconduct.

sentences.zh: 因乞骸骨。

translations.literal: He thereupon begged for his bones.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝為兩解之。

translations.literal: The emperor reconciled the two of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mediated between them.

sentences.zh: 一清又因災變請戒飭百官和衷，復乞宥議禮諸臣罪，璁益憾。

translations.literal: Yiqing again, because of calamities and anomalies, requested admonishing and ordering the hundred officials to harmony, and again begged pardon for the crimes of the ministers who debated the rites; Cong resented this all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing again cited omens and disasters to urge the officials to work in harmony and again asked pardon for those punished in the Rites controversy, deepening Zhang Cong's resentment.

sentences.zh: 柱萼入內閣，亦不相能。

translations.literal: Gui E entered the Grand Secretariat and likewise could not get along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E entered the Grand Secretariat and likewise could not work with him.

sentences.zh: 一清屢求去，且言：「今持論者尚紛更，臣獨主安靜；

translations.literal: Yiqing repeatedly sought to leave, and moreover said: 'Today those who hold opinions still favor constant change; your servant alone upholds quiet;
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing repeatedly asked to retire, saying, "Those who hold power today still favor constant change, while I alone uphold stability;

sentences.zh: 尚刻核，臣獨主寬平。

translations.literal: they still favor severity and scrutiny; your servant alone upholds leniency and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: they favor severity, while I alone uphold leniency and fairness.

sentences.zh: 用是多齟齬，願避賢者路。

translations.literal: Because of this there is much friction; I wish to yield the road to the worthy.'
translations.idiomatic: For this reason we are constantly at odds, and I wish to yield the road to worthier men."

sentences.zh: 」帝復溫旨褒之。

translations.literal: The emperor again issued warm words praising him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again responded with warm words of praise.

sentences.zh: 而給事中王準、陸粲發璁、萼招權納賄狀，帝立罷璁、萼，且暴其罪。

translations.literal: But supervising secretaries Wang Zhun and Lu Can exposed Cong and E's abuse of power and acceptance of bribes; the emperor immediately dismissed Cong and E and also exposed their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: But Supervising Secretaries Wang Zhun and Lu Can exposed Zhang Cong and Gui E for abuse of power and taking bribes; the emperor immediately dismissed them and publicly announced their crimes.

sentences.zh: 其黨霍韜攘臂曰：「張、桂行，勢且及我。

translations.literal: Their partisan Huo Tao rolled up his sleeves and said: 'If Zhang and Gui go, the momentum will reach me next.
translations.idiomatic: Their ally Huo Tao cried, "If Zhang and Gui fall, the blow will reach me next.

sentences.zh: 」遂上疏力攻一清，言其受張永、蕭敬賄。

translations.literal: ' He thereupon submitted a memorial forcefully attacking Yiqing, saying he had received bribes from Zhang Yong and Xiao Jing.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted a fierce memorial attacking Yiqing, accusing him of taking bribes from Zhang Yong and Xiao Jing.

sentences.zh: 一清再疏辨，乞罷。

translations.literal: Yiqing again memorialized in defense and begged dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing memorialized again in defense and asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝雖慰留之，而璁復召還，韜攻益急，且言法司承一清風指，構成萼罪。

translations.literal: Although the emperor comforted him and kept him, Cong was again recalled; Tao's attacks grew fiercer, and he also said the judiciary followed Yiqing's hints and fabricated E's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor comforted him and kept him at court, Zhang Cong was recalled; Huo Tao's attacks grew fiercer, and he charged that the judiciary followed Yiqing's direction in fabricating Gui E's guilt.

sentences.zh: 帝果怒，令法司會廷臣雜議。

translations.literal: The emperor was indeed enraged and ordered the judiciary to convene with court ministers for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was indeed enraged and ordered the judiciary to convene with court ministers for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 出刑部尚書周倫於南京，以侍郎許贊代。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Zhou Lun was sent out to Nanjing, and vice minister Xu Zan replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Zhou Lun was transferred to Nanjing and replaced by Vice Minister Xu Zan.

sentences.zh: 贊乃實韜言，請削一清籍。

translations.literal: Zan then verified Tao's words and requested stripping Yiqing of his registry.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zan then upheld Huo Tao's charges and recommended stripping Yiqing of his official rank.

sentences.zh: 帝令一清自陳。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yiqing to state his own case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yiqing to state his own case.

sentences.zh: 璁乃三上密疏，引一清贊禮功，乞賜寬假，實以堅帝意俾之去。

translations.literal: Cong then thrice submitted secret memorials, citing Yiqing's merit in supporting the rites and begging grace for him—in reality to firm the emperor's intent that he depart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong then submitted three secret memorials citing Yiqing's merit in the Rites controversy and begging leniency for him—in reality to harden the emperor's resolve that Yiqing should go.

sentences.zh: 帝果允致仕，馳驛歸，仍賜金幣。

translations.literal: The emperor indeed permitted retirement; he returned by express relay, and was still bestowed gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his retirement; he returned home by express relay and was still rewarded with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 明年，璁等構朱繼宗獄，坐一清受張永弟容金錢，為永誌墓，又與容世錦衣指揮，遂落職閑住。

translations.literal: The next year, Cong and others fabricated the Zhu Jizong case, implicating Yiqing for receiving money from Zhang Yong's younger brother Rong, composing Yong's tomb inscription, and making Rong's son a hereditary Embroidered Uniform commander; he was thus demoted and lived in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhang Cong and others fabricated the Zhu Jizong case, implicating Yiqing for taking money from Zhang Yong's brother Rong, composing Yong's tomb inscription, and securing a hereditary Embroidered Uniform command for Rong's son; Yiqing was demoted and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 一清大恨曰：「老矣，乃為孺子所賣！

translations.literal: Yiqing said with great hatred: 'I am old, yet sold out by a stripling!'
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing cried out in bitter anger, "I am old, yet sold out by a stripling!"

sentences.zh: 」疽發背死。

translations.literal: An abscess broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: An abscess broke out on his back and he died.

sentences.zh: 遺疏言身被汙蔑，死且不瞑，帝令釋贓罪不問。

translations.literal: His final memorial said his person had been slandered and he could not close his eyes in death; the emperor ordered the bribery charge released and not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: In his final memorial he wrote that he had been slandered and could not die in peace; the emperor ordered the bribery charge dropped.

sentences.zh: 後數年復故官。

translations.literal: Several years later his former office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 久之，贈太保，謚文襄。

translations.literal: After a long while he was posthumously given Grand Guardian and the posthumous name Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 一清生而隱宮，貌寺人，無子。

translations.literal: Yiqing was born with a hidden palace mark, his appearance like a eunuch, and had no son.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing was born with a hidden palace mark on his body, looked like a eunuch, and had no son.

sentences.zh: 博學善權變，尤曉暢邊事。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and skilled in flexible adaptation, especially thoroughly versed in frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and skilled in flexible adaptation, especially expert in frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 羽書旁午，一夕占十疏，悉中機宜。

translations.literal: When urgent dispatches came from all sides, in one night he drafted ten memorials, all hitting the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: When urgent dispatches arrived from all sides, he could draft ten memorials in a single night, each striking the right note.

sentences.zh: 人或訾己，反薦揚之。

translations.literal: If someone slandered him, he would instead recommend and praise them.
translations.idiomatic: If someone criticized him, he would recommend and praise them instead.

sentences.zh: 惟晚與璁、萼異，為所軋，不獲以恩禮終。

translations.literal: Only in his later years he differed from Cong and E and was crushed by them, not obtaining to end his days in favor and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Only in his later years did he fall out with Zhang Cong and Gui E; crushed by them, he was denied a gracious end.

sentences.zh: 然其才一時無兩，或比之姚崇雲。

translations.literal: Yet his talent had no second in his time; some compared him to Yao Chong and Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his talent had no equal in his day; some compared him to Yao Chong and Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 王瓊，字德華，太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiong, style name Dehua, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong, courtesy name Dehua, was a native of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 成化二十年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twentieth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1484.

sentences.zh: 授工部主事，進郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Works and advanced to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Works and later promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 出治漕河三年，臚其事為誌。

translations.literal: Sent out to administer the Grand Canal for three years, he set forth the affairs in a record.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to administer the Grand Canal for three years, he compiled a detailed record of the work.

sentences.zh: 繼者按稽之，不爽毫髮，由是以敏練稱。

translations.literal: His successor checked against it and not a hair's breadth was off; because of this he was known for keen efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: His successor checked his records and found not a hair's breadth of discrepancy; from this he gained a reputation for keen efficiency.

sentences.zh: 改戶部，歷河南右布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and served as right provincial administration commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and served as right provincial administration commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，擢右副都御史督漕運。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he was raised to right vice censor-in-chief supervising grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In 1506 he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief in charge of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 明年入為戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he entered service as right vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he entered the capital as right vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 衡府有賜地，蕪不可耕，勒民出租以為常，王反誣民趙賢等侵據。

translations.literal: The Princely Establishment of Heng had granted lands that were overgrown and uncultivable; the people were compelled to pay rent as a fixed rule, while the prince in turn falsely accused the people Zhao Xian and others of encroaching and seizing them.
translations.idiomatic: The Princely Establishment of Heng held granted lands that were overgrown and uncultivable; the people were compelled to pay rent as a fixed obligation, while the prince in turn falsely accused Zhao Xian and others of encroaching on the land.

sentences.zh: 瓊往按，奪旁近民地予之，賢等戍邊，民多怨者。

translations.literal: Qiong went to investigate, seized nearby commoners' lands and gave them to the prince; Xian and others were garrisoned on the frontier, and many among the people resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong went to investigate, seized nearby commoners' lands and gave them to the prince; Zhao Xian and others were sent to frontier garrison duty, and many people resented the decision.

sentences.zh: 三年春，廷推吏部侍郎，前後六人，皆不允。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year, the court recommended candidates for vice minister of personnel; six men in succession were all not approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of his third year, six candidates in succession were recommended for vice minister of personnel, and all were rejected.

sentences.zh: 最後以瓊上，許之。

translations.literal: Finally Qiong was put forward and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Finally Wang Qiong was put forward and approved.

sentences.zh: 坐任戶部時邊臣借太倉銀未償，所司奏遲，尚書顧佐奪俸，而瓊改南京。

translations.literal: Because while serving in the Ministry of Revenue frontier officials had borrowed silver from the Taicang treasury without repaying, and the responsible office reported late, Minister Gu Zuo had his salary taken and Qiong was transferred to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Because frontier officials had borrowed silver from the Taicang treasury without repaying during his tenure at the Ministry of Revenue, and the responsible office reported late, Minister Gu Zuo had his salary docked and Qiong was transferred to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 已，復改戶部。

translations.literal: Before long he was again transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred back to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年進尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was advanced to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In his eighth year he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 瓊為人有心計，善鉤校。

translations.literal: Qiong as a man was calculating and skilled at audit and verification.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was calculating by nature and skilled at auditing accounts.

sentences.zh: 為郎時悉錄故牘條例，盡得其斂散盈縮狀。

translations.literal: When a bureau secretary he recorded all old documents and regulations in full, mastering the state of intake, outflow, surplus, and shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: As a bureau secretary he copied out all old documents and regulations, mastering every detail of revenue intake, expenditure, surplus, and shortfall.

sentences.zh: 及為尚書，益明習國計。

translations.literal: When he became minister, he grew even more thoroughly versed in national finance.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became minister, he grew even more expert in national finance.

sentences.zh: 邊帥請芻糗，則屈指計某倉、某場庤糧草幾何；

translations.literal: When frontier commanders requested fodder and grain, he would count on his fingers and calculate how much grain and fodder were stored in such-and-such a granary or depot;
translations.idiomatic: When frontier commanders requested fodder and grain, he would reckon on his fingers how much was stored in each granary and depot;

sentences.zh: 諸郡歲輸、邊卒歲采秋青幾何，曰：「足矣。

translations.literal: how much the various prefectures delivered annually and how much autumn forage the frontier troops gathered, and say: 'It is enough.
translations.idiomatic: how much each prefecture delivered annually and how much autumn forage the frontier troops collected, and say, "That is enough.

sentences.zh: 重索妄也。

translations.literal: To demand more would be reckless.'
translations.idiomatic: To demand more would be unjust."

sentences.zh: 」人益以瓊為才。

translations.literal: People all the more regarded Qiong as talented.
translations.idiomatic: People regarded Qiong as even more capable.

sentences.zh: 十年代陸完為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he replaced Lu Wan as minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he replaced Lu Wan as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時四方盜起，將士以首功進秩。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose in all directions, and officers and soldiers advanced in rank by counted heads.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandits rose throughout the empire, and officers and soldiers were promoted by the number of enemy heads they claimed.

sentences.zh: 瓊言：「此嬴秦弊政。

translations.literal: Qiong said: 'This is the corrupt policy of rapacious Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong said, "This is the corrupt Qin-dynasty policy.

sentences.zh: 行之邊方猶可，未有內地而論首功者。

translations.literal: To apply it on the frontier may still be permissible; there has never been discussion of head-count merit in the interior.
translations.idiomatic: It may still be applied on the frontier, but head-count merit has never been used in the interior provinces.

sentences.zh: 今江西、四川妄殺平民千萬，縱賊貽禍，皆此議所致。

translations.literal: Now in Jiangxi and Sichuan they recklessly kill countless thousands of civilians, let bandits escape and leave calamity behind—all caused by this policy.
translations.idiomatic: Now in Jiangxi and Sichuan countless civilians are killed without cause, bandits are allowed to escape and leave disaster behind—all because of this policy.

sentences.zh: 自今內地征討，惟以蕩平為功，不計首級。

translations.literal: From now on, for campaigns in the interior, only complete pacification shall count as merit; heads shall not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, for interior campaigns, only complete pacification shall count as merit; enemy heads shall not be counted.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 帝時遠遊塞外，經歲不還，近畿盜竊發。

translations.literal: The emperor at the time traveled far beyond the frontier for long periods without returning, and bandits and thieves arose in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at the time made extended tours beyond the frontier and was away for a year at a time, while theft and banditry broke out near the capital.

sentences.zh: 瓊請於河間設總兵一人，大名、武定各設兵備副使一人，責以平賊，而檄順天、保定兩巡撫，嚴要害為外防，集遼東、延綏士馬於行在，以護軍駕。

translations.literal: Qiong requested that a regional commander be stationed at Hejian, and that military intendants be placed at Daming and Wuding, charged with pacifying bandits; he also ordered the grand coordinators of Shuntian and Baoding to guard strategic points as outer defense, and assembled Liaodong and Yan-sui troops at the temporary palace to protect the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong proposed stationing a regional commander at Hejian and military intendants at Daming and Wuding to suppress bandits; he ordered the grand coordinators of Shuntian and Baoding to guard key passes, and assembled troops from Liaodong and Yan-sui at the temporary palace to protect the emperor.

sentences.zh: 中外恃以無恐。

translations.literal: Within and without the court relied on this and were unafraid.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike took comfort and were unafraid.

sentences.zh: 孝豐賊湯麻九反，有司請發兵剿。

translations.literal: At Xiaofeng, bandit Tang Majiu rebelled; the responsible officials requested dispatching troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaofeng the bandit Tang Majiu rebelled, and local officials requested troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 瓊請密敕勘糧都御史許廷光，出不意擒之，無一脫者。

translations.literal: Qiong requested a secret edict to grain-inspection censor-in-chief Xu Tingguang to take them unawares and capture them; not one escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong asked for a secret edict to Grain-Inspection Censor-in-Chief Xu Tingguang to seize them by surprise; not one escaped.

sentences.zh: 四方捷奏上，多推功瓊，數受蔭賚，累加至少師兼太子太師，子錦衣世千戶。

translations.literal: Victory reports arrived from all directions, mostly attributing merit to Qiong; he repeatedly received hereditary rewards and was cumulatively advanced to Junior Preceptor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with his son enrolled as hereditary commander of one thousand Embroidered Uniform households.
translations.idiomatic: Victory reports from all directions mostly credited Qiong; he received repeated hereditary rewards and rose to Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with his son enrolled as a hereditary commander of one thousand Embroidered Uniform households.

sentences.zh: 及營建乾清宮，又蔭錦衣千戶者二，寵遇冠諸尚書。

translations.literal: When the Qianqing Palace was built, two more hereditary Embroidered Uniform households of one thousand each were granted; his favor exceeded that of all other ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianqing Palace was constructed, two more hereditary Embroidered Uniform commands of one thousand households each were granted; his favor surpassed all other ministers.

sentences.zh: 十四年，寧王宸濠反。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Prince Ning Zhu Chenhao rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 瓊請敕南和伯方壽祥督操江兵防南都，南贛巡撫王守仁、湖廣巡撫秦金各率所部趨南昌，應天巡撫李充嗣鎮京口，淮揚巡撫叢蘭扼儀真。

translations.literal: Qiong requested an edict ordering the Earl of Nanhe Fang Shouxiang to supervise river-defense troops to protect the southern capital; Nan-Gan Grand Coordinator Wang Shouren and Huguang Grand Coordinator Qin Jin each to lead their forces toward Nanchang; Yingtian Grand Coordinator Li Chongsi to guard Jingkou; and Huai-Yang Grand Coordinator Cong Lan to block Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong proposed an edict ordering the Earl of Nanhe Fang Shouxiang to command river-defense troops to protect Nanjing; Nan-Gan Grand Coordinator Wang Shouren and Huguang Grand Coordinator Qin Jin to march on Nanchang; Yingtian Grand Coordinator Li Chongsi to guard Jingkou; and Huai-Yang Grand Coordinator Cong Lan to block Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 奏上，帝意欲親征，持三日不下。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor wished to campaign in person; he held it for three days without issuing a decision.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor wished to campaign in person and withheld approval for three days.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊廷和趣之，竟下親征詔，命瓊與廷和等居守。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe urged him, and the edict for the personal campaign was finally issued, ordering Qiong and Tinghe and others to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe pressed him, and the edict for a personal campaign was finally issued, with Qiong and Tinghe ordered to remain and guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，瓊用王守仁撫南、贛，假便宜提督軍務。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qiong had employed Wang Shouren to pacify southern Ganzhou, granting him discretionary authority as overall military supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qiong had appointed Wang Shouren to pacify southern Ganzhou with discretionary authority as overall military supervisor.

sentences.zh: 比宸濠反，書聞，舉朝惴惴。

translations.literal: When Chenhao rebelled and the report arrived, the whole court was fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When news of Chenhao's rebellion arrived, the whole court was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 瓊曰：「諸君勿憂，吾用王伯安贛州，正為今日，賊旦夕擒耳。

translations.literal: Qiong said: 'Gentlemen, do not worry. I employed Wang Bo'an in Ganzhou precisely for this day; the bandit will be captured within days.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong said, "Do not worry, gentlemen. I placed Wang Shouren in Ganzhou precisely for this day; the rebel will be captured within days.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，果如其言。

translations.literal: Before long it indeed happened as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Before long events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 瓊才高，善結納。

translations.literal: Qiong was talented and skilled at forming connections.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was highly capable and skilled at cultivating connections.

sentences.zh: 厚事錢寧、江彬等，因得自展，所奏請輒行。

translations.literal: He treated Qian Ning, Jiang Bin, and others generously and thereby gained scope for his own designs; whatever he memorialized was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished favors on Qian Ning, Jiang Bin, and their faction and thereby gained room to act; his memorials were generally approved.

sentences.zh: 其能為功於兵部者，亦彬等力也。

translations.literal: What he could accomplish in the Ministry of War was also due to Bin and the others' power.
translations.idiomatic: What he achieved as minister of war owed much to Bin and his allies.

sentences.zh: 陸完敗，代為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Lu Wan was defeated, Qiong replaced him as minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Wan fell, Qiong replaced him as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 瓊忌彭澤平流賊，聲望出己上，構於錢寧，中澤危法。

translations.literal: Qiong resented that Peng Ze had pacified the river bandits and that his reputation stood above his own; he framed Ze through Qian Ning and trapped him with a capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong resented Peng Ze for pacifying the river bandits and surpassing him in reputation; he framed Ze through Qian Ning and nearly had him executed.

sentences.zh: 又陷雲南巡撫範鏞、甘肅巡撫李昆、副使陳九疇於獄，中外多畏瓊。

translations.literal: He also trapped Yunnan Grand Coordinator Fan Yong, Gansu Grand Coordinator Li Kun, and vice commissioner Chen Jiuchou in prison; many within and without the court feared Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Yunnan Grand Coordinator Fan Yong, Gansu Grand Coordinator Li Kun, and Vice Commissioner Chen Jiuchou imprisoned; many at court and beyond feared him.

sentences.zh: 而大學士廷和亦以瓊所誅賞，多取中旨，不關內閣，弗能堪。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Tinghe also could not bear that in rewards and punishments Qiong mostly took direct edicts and did not go through the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe also resented that Qiong's rewards and punishments mostly followed direct edicts without Grand Secretariat review.

sentences.zh: 明年，世宗入繼，言官交劾瓊，系都察院獄。

translations.literal: The next year, when Emperor Shizong succeeded, censorial officials impeached Qiong in succession and he was imprisoned in the Censorate jail.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Emperor Shizong succeeded, censorial officials impeached Qiong in succession and he was imprisoned in the Censorate jail.

sentences.zh: 瓊力訐廷和，帝愈不直瓊，下廷臣雜議。

translations.literal: Qiong strenuously accused Tinghe; the emperor was all the less favorable to Qiong and ordered court ministers to deliberate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong attacked Tinghe fiercely; the emperor was all the less disposed in his favor and ordered a joint deliberation by court ministers.

sentences.zh: 坐交結近侍律論死，命戍莊浪。

translations.literal: He was sentenced under the statute on associating with imperial favorites and condemned to death, then ordered exiled to Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted under the statute on associating with imperial favorites and sentenced to death, then ordered exiled to Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 瓊復訴年老，改戍綏德。

translations.literal: Qiong again pleaded old age and was changed to exile at Suide.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong again pleaded old age and was transferred to exile at Suide.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼、霍韜用事，以瓊與廷和仇，首薦之，不納。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Huo Tao held power, because Qiong was hostile to Tinghe they recommended him first, but he was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Huo Tao held power, they recommended Qiong first because of his feud with Tinghe, but the appointment was not made.

sentences.zh: 至嘉靖六年有邊警，萼力請用瓊，不果。

translations.literal: By the sixth year of Jiajing there was a frontier alarm; Gui E strenuously requested using Qiong, but it did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiajing a frontier alarm arose; Gui E pressed hard to employ Qiong, but without success.

sentences.zh: 帝亦憫瓊老病，令還籍為民。

translations.literal: The emperor also pitied Qiong's age and illness and ordered him returned to his native place as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also pitied Qiong's age and illness and ordered him returned home as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 御史胡松因劾萼謫外任，其同官周在請宥松，並下詔獄。

translations.literal: Censor Hu Song was demoted for impeaching Gui E; his colleague Zhou Zai asked pardon for Song, and both were sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hu Song was demoted for impeaching Gui E; his colleague Zhou Zai asked pardon for Song, and both were sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 萼復言瓊前攻廷和，故廷臣群起排之。

translations.literal: Gui E again said that because Qiong had formerly attacked Tinghe, court ministers had risen in a body to exclude him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E again argued that because Qiong had attacked Tinghe, court ministers had banded together to exclude him.

sentences.zh: 帝乃命復瓊尚書待用。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon ordered Qiong's ministerial rank restored for future use.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Qiong's ministerial rank restored for future employment.

sentences.zh: 明年遂以兵部尚書兼右都御史代王憲督陜西三邊軍務。

translations.literal: The next year he was made minister of war and concurrently right censor-in-chief in place of Wang Xian to supervise military affairs on Shaanxi's three frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed minister of war and right censor-in-chief in place of Wang Xian to supervise military affairs on Shaanxi's three frontiers.

sentences.zh: 土魯番據哈密，廷議閉關絕其貢，四年矣。

translations.literal: Turpan held Hami; the court had debated closing the border and cutting off their tribute for four years.
translations.idiomatic: Turpan held Hami, and the court had closed the border and cut off tribute for four years.

sentences.zh: 至是，其將牙木蘭為酋速檀滿速兒所疑，率從二千求內屬。

translations.literal: By then their general Yalansha, suspected by the chief Shaytans Mansuer, led two thousand followers to seek submission within the border.
translations.idiomatic: By then their general Yalansha, suspected by the chief Shaytans Mansuer, led two thousand followers to seek submission within the border.

sentences.zh: 沙州番人帖木哥、土巴等，素為土魯番役屬者，苦其征求，亦率五千余人入附。

translations.literal: Shazhou tribesmen Tiemuge, Tuba, and others, who had long been subject to Turpan and suffered their exactions, also led more than five thousand people to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Shazhou tribesmen Tiemuge, Tuba, and others, long subject to Turpan and worn down by their levies, also led more than five thousand people to submit.

sentences.zh: 番人來寇，連為參將雲昌等所敗。

translations.literal: When the tribes came to raid, they were repeatedly defeated by Regional Commander Yun Chang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal raiders were repeatedly defeated by Regional Commander Yun Chang and others.

sentences.zh: 其引瓦剌寇肅州者，遊擊彭濬擊退之。

translations.literal: Those who led Oirat raiders against Suzhou were repulsed by Mobile Corps Commander Peng Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Those who led Oirat raiders against Suzhou were repulsed by Mobile Corps Commander Peng Jun.

sentences.zh: 賊既失援，又數失利，乃獻還哈密。

translations.literal: Having lost support and suffered repeated defeats, they then returned Hami.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost their allies and suffered repeated defeats, they then returned Hami.

sentences.zh: 求通貢，乞歸羈留使臣，而語多謾。

translations.literal: They sought to resume tribute and begged return of detained envoys, but their words were mostly insolent.
translations.idiomatic: They sought to resume tribute and asked for the return of detained envoys, but their language was mostly insolent.

sentences.zh: 瓊奏乞撫納，帝從兵部尚書王時中議，如瓊請。

translations.literal: Qiong memorialized requesting pacification and acceptance; the emperor followed Minister of War Wang Shizhong's deliberation and approved Qiong's request.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong memorialized asking to pacify and accept them; the emperor followed Minister of War Wang Shizhong's recommendation and approved Qiong's request.

sentences.zh: 霍韜難之，瓊再疏請詔還番使，通貢如故。

translations.literal: Huo Tao objected; Qiong again memorialized requesting an edict to return the tribal envoys and restore tribute as before.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Tao objected; Qiong memorialized again asking for an edict to return the tribal envoys and restore tribute as before.

sentences.zh: 自是西域復定，而北寇常為邊患。

translations.literal: From this the western regions were again settled, while northern raiders remained a constant frontier trouble.
translations.idiomatic: From this the western regions were pacified again, while northern raiders remained a constant frontier threat.

sentences.zh: 初入犯莊浪，瓊部諸將遮擊之，斬數十級。

translations.literal: On first invading, they entered Zhuanglang; Qiong's subordinate generals intercepted them and beheaded several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: When they first invaded Zhuanglang, Qiong's generals intercepted them and beheaded several dozen.
