sentences.zh: 俄由紅城子入，殺部餉主簿張文明。

translations.literal: Soon they entered by Hongchengzi and killed provisions clerk Zhang Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they entered through Hongchengzi and killed provisions clerk Zhang Wenming.

sentences.zh: 明年以數萬騎寇寧夏。

translations.literal: The next year they raided Ningxia with tens of thousands of horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they raided Ningxia with tens of thousands of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 已又犯靈州，瓊督遊擊梁震等邀斬七十余人。

translations.literal: They then attacked Lingzhou; Qiong supervised Mobile Corps Commander Liang Zhen and others in an ambush and beheaded more than seventy.
translations.idiomatic: They then attacked Lingzhou; Qiong directed Mobile Corps Commander Liang Zhen and others to ambush them and behead more than seventy.

sentences.zh: 其秋，集諸道精卒三萬，按行塞下。

translations.literal: That autumn he assembled thirty thousand picked troops from all routes and inspected the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he assembled thirty thousand picked troops from all routes and inspected the frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 寇聞，徙帳遠遁。

translations.literal: When the raiders heard of this, they moved their camps far away.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders heard of this, they moved their camps far away.

sentences.zh: 諸軍分道出，縱野燒，耀兵而還。

translations.literal: The armies marched out by separate routes, set fires across the open country, displayed their strength, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The armies marched out by separate routes, burned the open country, displayed their strength, and returned.

sentences.zh: 先是，南京給事中邱九仞劾瓊，帝慰留之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Nanjing supervising secretary Qiu Jiuren had impeached Qiong, and the emperor comforted him and kept him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Nanjing Supervising Secretary Qiu Jiuren had impeached Qiong, and the emperor comforted him and kept him at his post.

sentences.zh: 及璁、萼罷政，諸劾璁、萼黨者鹹首瓊，乃令致仕。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cong and Gui E left office, those who had impeached their faction all named Qiong first, and he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong and Gui E fell from power, those who had impeached their faction named Qiong first, and he was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 俄寢前詔，遣慰諭。

translations.literal: Before long the earlier edict was suspended and envoys were sent to console him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the retirement edict was suspended and envoys were sent to console him.

sentences.zh: 會番大掠臨洮，瓊集兵討若籠、板爾諸族，焚其巢，斬首三百六十，撫降七十余族。

translations.literal: When tribes raided Lintao on a large scale, Qiong assembled troops to attack the Ruolong and Ban'er clans, burned their nests, beheaded three hundred sixty, and pacified more than seventy clans.
translations.idiomatic: When tribes raided Lintao on a large scale, Qiong assembled troops against the Ruolong and Ban'er clans, burned their camps, beheaded three hundred sixty, and pacified more than seventy clans.

sentences.zh: 錄功，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded and he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded and he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 瓊在邊，戎備甚飭。

translations.literal: While Qiong was on the frontier, military preparedness was very strict.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier Qiong maintained very strict military discipline.

sentences.zh: 寇嘗入山西得利，逾歲復獵境上，陽欲東，瓊令備其西。

translations.literal: The raiders once entered Shanxi with profit; more than a year later they hunted along the border again, feigning an eastern move, and Qiong ordered defenses to the west.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders once raided Shanxi with success; more than a year later they prowled the border again, feigning an eastern thrust, and Qiong ordered defenses to the west.

sentences.zh: 寇果入，大敗之。

translations.literal: The raiders indeed entered and were heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders entered as he expected and were heavily defeated.

sentences.zh: 諸番蕩平，西陲益靖。

translations.literal: The tribes were swept clean and the western marches grew ever more tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were pacified and the western frontier grew tranquil.

sentences.zh: 甘肅軍民素苦土魯番侵暴，恐瓊去，相率乞守臣奏留。

translations.literal: The people of Gansu had long suffered Turpan's invasions and feared that if Qiong left, they would petition local officials to request his retention.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Gansu had long suffered Turpan's raids and, fearing Qiong's departure, petitioned through local officials to keep him.

sentences.zh: 於是巡撫唐澤、巡按胡明善具陳其功，乞如軍民請。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Coordinator Tang Ze and Investigating Censor Hu Mingshan fully set forth his merit and asked as the people requested.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Tang Ze and Investigating Censor Hu Mingshan then detailed his achievements and supported the people's request.

sentences.zh: 優詔獎之。

translations.literal: A gracious edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 初，帝惡楊廷和，疑廷臣悉其黨，故連用桂萼、方獻夫為吏部。

translations.literal: At first the emperor disliked Yang Tinghe and suspected that court ministers were all his partisans, so he repeatedly used Gui E and Fang Xianfu as ministers of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor disliked Yang Tinghe and suspected court ministers were all his partisans, so he repeatedly appointed Gui E and Fang Xianfu as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 及獻夫去，帝不欲授他人，久不補。

translations.literal: When Xianfu departed, the emperor did not wish to give the post to anyone else and long left it unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianfu left, the emperor did not wish to appoint anyone else and left the post vacant for a long time.

sentences.zh: 至十年冬，遣行人賫敕召瓊為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: By the winter of the tenth year he dispatched an envoy bearing an edict to summon Qiong as minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: By the winter of the tenth year he sent an envoy with an edict summoning Qiong as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 南京御史馬敭等十人力詆瓊先朝遺奸。

translations.literal: Ten Nanjing censors including Ma Yang and others strenuously denounced Qiong as a surviving villain of the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: Ten Nanjing censors including Ma Yang strenuously denounced Qiong as a surviving villain of the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，盡逮敭等下詔獄，慰諭瓊。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, had Yang and the others all arrested and sent to the imperial prison, and comforted Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, had Yang and the others arrested and sent to the imperial prison, and comforted Qiong.

sentences.zh: 未凡，敭等亦還職。

translations.literal: Before long Yang and the others also returned to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang and the others were also restored to their posts.

sentences.zh: 花馬池有警，兵部尚書王憲請發兵。

translations.literal: When there was an alarm at Huama Chi, Minister of War Wang Xian requested dispatching troops.
translations.idiomatic: When there was an alarm at Huama Chi, Minister of War Wang Xian requested troops.

sentences.zh: 瓊言花馬池備嚴，寇不能入，大軍至，且先退，徒耗中國。

translations.literal: Qiong said that Huama Chi's defenses were strict and raiders could not enter; when a great army arrived they would withdraw first, wasting the empire's resources in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong said Huama Chi was well defended and raiders could not penetrate; a large army would arrive only after they had withdrawn, wasting imperial resources.

sentences.zh: 憲竟發六千人，比至彰德，寇果遁。

translations.literal: Xian still dispatched six thousand men; by the time they reached Zhangde the raiders had indeed fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian still dispatched six thousand men; by the time they reached Zhangde the raiders had fled.

sentences.zh: 明年秋卒官。

translations.literal: The next autumn he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚恭襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Preceptor and the posthumous name Gongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Gongxiang.

sentences.zh: 是年，彭澤已先卒矣。

translations.literal: That year Peng Ze had already died before him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Peng Ze had already died before him.

sentences.zh: 當正、嘉間，澤、瓊並有才略，相中傷不已，亦叠為進退。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde and Jiajing reigns, Ze and Qiong were both talented and strategic and ceaselessly undermined each other, also rising and falling in turn.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde and Jiajing reigns, Peng Ze and Qiong were both talented strategists who ceaselessly undermined each other and rose and fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 而瓊險忮，公論尤不予。

translations.literal: Yet Qiong was treacherous and jealous, and public opinion especially did not favor him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qiong was treacherous and jealous, and public opinion especially disapproved of him.

sentences.zh: 然在本兵時功多。

translations.literal: Yet while he held the Ministry of War he accomplished much.
translations.idiomatic: Yet while he held the Ministry of War he accomplished a great deal.

sentences.zh: 而其督三邊也，人以比楊一清雲。

translations.literal: And in supervising the three frontiers, people compared him to Yang Yiqing.
translations.idiomatic: In supervising the three frontiers, people compared him to Yang Yiqing.

sentences.zh: 彭澤，字濟物，蘭州人。

translations.literal: Peng Ze, style name Jiwu, was a man of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze, courtesy name Jiwu, was a native of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼學於外祖段堅，有誌節。

translations.literal: In youth he studied with his maternal grandfather Duan Jian and possessed resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied with his maternal grandfather Duan Jian and possessed firm resolve and integrity.

sentences.zh: 會試二場畢，聞母病，徑歸，母病亦已。

translations.literal: He had finished the second session of the metropolitan examination when he heard his mother was ill; he went straight home, and his mother's illness had already passed.
translations.idiomatic: He had finished the second session of the metropolitan examination when he heard his mother was ill; he went straight home, and found her already recovered.

sentences.zh: 登弘治三年進士，授工部主事，歷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He attained jinshi rank in the third year of Hongzhi and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Works, serving through director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1490, was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Works, and rose to director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 勢豪殺人，澤置之辟。

translations.literal: When a powerful family murdered someone, Ze sentenced him to capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When a powerful family committed murder, Ze sentenced the killer to death.

sentences.zh: 中貴為祈免，執不聽。

translations.literal: A palace eunuch interceded for pardon, but he held firm and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch interceded for pardon, but he stood firm and refused.

sentences.zh: 出為徽州知府。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 澤將遣女，治漆器數十，使吏送其家。

translations.literal: Ze was about to send off his daughter and had several dozen pieces of lacquerware prepared, ordering clerks to deliver them to his home.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Ze was preparing to marry off his daughter, he had several dozen lacquer objects made and sent clerks to carry them to his family home.

sentences.zh: 澤父大怒，趣焚之，徒步詣徽。

translations.literal: Ze's father was greatly angered, urged that they be burned, and went on foot to Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father flew into a rage, had the lacquerware burned, and walked the whole way to Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 澤驚出迓，自吏負其裝。

translations.literal: Ze, startled, went out to meet him and himself carried his father’s baggage from the clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze hurried out to welcome him, took his father’s luggage from the clerk, and carried it himself.

sentences.zh: 父怒曰：「吾負此數千里，汝不能負數步耶？

translations.literal: His father said angrily, “I carried this several thousand li—can you not carry it a few paces?”
translations.idiomatic: His father thundered, “I bore this load thousands of li—are you unable to carry it a few steps?”

sentences.zh: 」入，杖澤堂下。

translations.literal: ” He entered and beat Ze below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went inside and had Peng Ze flogged in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 杖已，持裝徑去。

translations.literal: When the beating was done, he took the baggage and went straight away.
translations.idiomatic: When the flogging ended, he shouldered the luggage and left without another word.

sentences.zh: 澤益痛砥礪。

translations.literal: Ze grieved all the more and strove to improve himself.
translations.idiomatic: The humiliation cut deep, and Peng Ze redoubled his efforts at self-discipline.

sentences.zh: 政最，人以方前守孫遇。

translations.literal: His administration ranked highest; people compared him to the former prefect Sun Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was rated the finest in the province, and contemporaries ranked him with the celebrated prefect Sun Yu.

sentences.zh: 遇見《循吏傳》中。

translations.literal: Yu appears in the “Diligent Officials” biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yu himself is commemorated in the “Diligent Officials” section of the histories.

sentences.zh: 父喪歸。

translations.literal: When his father died, he returned home for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning when his father died.

sentences.zh: 正德初，起知真定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign, he was recalled to serve as prefect of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde era he was recalled and appointed prefect of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 閹人數撓禁，澤治一棺於廳事，以死怵之，其人不敢逞。

translations.literal: Eunuchs repeatedly violated prohibitions; Ze had a coffin set up in the main hall and intimidated them with death, and they did not dare act outrageously.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs kept breaking local rules, he placed a coffin in the reception hall and threatened offenders with death—after that they dared not abuse their power.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江副使，歷河南按察使，所至以威猛稱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, then served as Surveillance Commissioner of Henan; wherever he went he was known for fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice commissioner in Zhejiang and later surveillance commissioner in Henan, he earned a reputation for relentless severity wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 擢右僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and was appointed grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史，改保定。

translations.literal: He advanced to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and was reassigned to Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Further promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, he was transferred to Baoding.

sentences.zh: 未赴，而劉惠、趙鐩等亂河南，命澤與鹹寧伯仇鉞提督軍務討之。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post, Liu Hui, Zhao Zhen, and others rebelled in Henan; Ze was ordered, together with the Earl of Xianning Qiu Yue, to supervise military affairs and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet assumed the Baoding post when Liu Hui and Zhao Zhen rose in Henan; the court ordered Peng Ze and the Earl of Xianning, Qiu Yue, to take joint command and crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 陳便宜十一事，厚賞峻罰，以激勸將吏。

translations.literal: He set forth eleven expedient proposals, with rich rewards and harsh punishments, to rouse and encourage officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted eleven practical proposals pairing generous rewards with stern punishments to galvanize officers and troops.

sentences.zh: 澤體幹修偉，腰帶十二圍，大音聲，與人語若叱咤。

translations.literal: Ze’s physique was tall and imposing; his belt measured twelve circumferences; his voice was loud, and when he spoke to others it was like shouting.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze was a towering man with a twelve-fold belt girth, a booming voice, and a manner of address that sounded like a battlefield roar.

sentences.zh: 始至，大陳軍容，引見諸將校，責以畏縮當死。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, he arrayed the army in great formation, summoned all the officers for audience, and rebuked them for cowardice, saying they deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he paraded the full army, summoned every commander, and denounced them for timidity, declaring them worthy of execution.

sentences.zh: 諸將校股栗伏罪，良久乃釋。

translations.literal: The officers trembled in their legs and pleaded guilty; only after a long while did he release them.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders shook with fear and confessed their fault; he kept them in suspense a long while before letting them go.

sentences.zh: 遂下令鼓行薄賊，大小數十戰，連破之。

translations.literal: He then ordered drums to beat advance and closed with the bandits; in several dozen battles large and small he defeated them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered a general advance, engaged the rebels in dozens of clashes, and broke them battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 甫四月，賊盡平，語詳《鉞傳》。

translations.literal: In only four months the bandits were entirely pacified; the account is given in detail in the biography of Qiu Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Within four months the rebels were wholly suppressed; the campaigns are narrated at length in Qiu Yue’s biography.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進右都御史、太子少保，蔭子錦衣世百戶。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his son was granted hereditary enrollment as a hundred-household commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards followed: he became Right Censor-in-Chief and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his son received a hereditary post as hundred-household commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋代洪鐘總督川、陜諸軍，討四川賊。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Hong Zhong as supreme commander of the armies of Sichuan and Shaanxi to campaign against the bandits of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he succeeded Hong Zhong as supreme commander of Sichuan and Shaanxi forces to quell brigandage in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時鄢本恕、藍廷瑞、廖惠、曹甫已平，惟廖麻子、喻思俸猖獗如故。

translations.literal: By then Yan Benshu, Lan Tingrui, Liao Hui, and Cao Fu had already been pacified; only Liao Mazi and Yu Sifu still ravaged as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Benshu, Lan Tingrui, Liao Hui, and Cao Fu were already subdued; only Liao Mazi and Yu Sifu still rampaged unchecked.

sentences.zh: 澤偕總兵官時源數敗賊，部將閻勛追擒麻子於劍州。

translations.literal: Ze, together with the regional commander Shi Yuan, repeatedly defeated the bandits; the subordinate general Yan Xun pursued and captured Mazi at Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze and regional commander Shi Yuan won repeated victories; subordinate Yan Xun ran down Liao Mazi and captured him at Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 思俸竄通、巴間，勢復振。

translations.literal: Sifu fled into the region between Tong and Ba, and their power revived.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Sifu slipped into the Tong–Ba country, and rebel strength surged again.

sentences.zh: 澤督諸軍圍之，卒就擒。

translations.literal: Ze directed the various armies to surround him, and in the end he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze encircled him with combined forces until he was taken at last.

sentences.zh: 澤遂移漢中，請班師。

translations.literal: Ze then shifted headquarters to Hanzhong and requested withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his headquarters to Hanzhong and asked permission to withdraw the troops.

sentences.zh: 未報，而內江、榮昌賊復熾，澤又移師討平之。

translations.literal: Before a reply came, bandits in Neijiang and Rongchang flared up again, and Ze once more shifted his army and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Before the court answered, unrest reignited in Neijiang and Rongchang, and he marched out again and crushed it.

sentences.zh: 且平成都亂卒之執知州、指揮者。

translations.literal: He also pacified the mutinous soldiers at Chengdu who had seized the prefect and a commander.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise put down Chengdu mutineers who had taken the prefect and a military commander hostage.

sentences.zh: 請班師益力，詔暫留保寧鎮撫。

translations.literal: He pressed all the harder to request withdrawal; an edict ordered him to remain temporarily at Baoning to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded more urgently to come home; the throne instead told him to stay at Baoning and settle the province.

sentences.zh: 進左都御史、太子太保，蔭子如初。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his son received the same hereditary privilege as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Left Censor-in-Chief and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the same hereditary honors for his son.

sentences.zh: 澤復請還者再，乃召還。

translations.literal: Ze twice more asked to return, and only then was he summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze petitioned twice more to retire before the court finally recalled him.

sentences.zh: 未行，會土魯番據哈密，執忠順王速檀拜牙郎，以其印去，投謾書甘肅，要索金幣。

translations.literal: Before he set out, Turpan seized Hami, seized the loyal-and-obedient king Sultan Bayandorji, took his seal, sent an insulting letter to Gansu, and demanded gold and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, Turpan occupied Hami, captured the loyal king Sultan Bayandorji, carried off his seal, sent a contemptuous missive to Gansu, and demanded gold and tribute.

sentences.zh: 總制鄧璋、甘肅巡撫趙鑒以聞，請遣大臣經略。

translations.literal: Supreme commander Deng Zhang and Gansu grand coordinator Zhao Jian reported this and asked that a senior minister be sent to take strategic command.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commander Deng Zhang and Gansu grand coordinator Zhao Jian memorialized the crisis and urged dispatch of a senior minister to direct policy on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊廷和等共薦澤。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretaries Yang Tinghe and others jointly recommended Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries led by Yang Tinghe united in recommending Peng Ze.

sentences.zh: 澤久在兵間，厭之。

translations.literal: Ze had long been among troops and was weary of it.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze had spent years in the field and loathed returning to war.

sentences.zh: 以鄉土為辭，且引疾，推璋及鹹寧侯鉞可任。

translations.literal: He pleaded his native region and also cited illness, recommending that Zhang and the Marquis of Xianning Qiu Yue could fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded distance from home and ill health, naming Deng Zhang and the Marquis of Xianning, Qiu Yue, as better choices.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔慰勉，乃行。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict of comfort and encouragement, and only then did he set out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a warm edict of encouragement, and Peng Ze at last departed.

sentences.zh: 澤材武知兵，然性疏闊負氣。

translations.literal: Ze was talented in arms and knew warfare, yet by nature he was broad and proud.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze was capable in military affairs, but his temperament was blunt and headstrong.

sentences.zh: 經略哈密事頗不當，錢寧、王瓊等交齮龁之，遂因此得罪。

translations.literal: His handling of the Hami campaign was rather improper; Qian Ning, Wang Qiong, and others joined in slandering and undermining him, and he thus fell into guilt.
translations.idiomatic: His Hami strategy misfired; Qian Ning and Wang Qiong piled on with mutual slander until he was ruined.

sentences.zh: 澤至甘州，土魯番方寇赤斤、苦峪諸衛，遣使索金幣，請還哈密。

translations.literal: When Ze reached Ganzhou, Turpan was then raiding the guards of Chijin and Kuyu and others, sending envoys to demand gold and goods and to ask that Hami be returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Ganzhou he found Turpan raiding Chijin, Kuyu, and neighboring guards while envoys demanded bullion and the restoration of Hami.

sentences.zh: 澤以番人可利啖也，與鑒謀，遣哈密都督寫亦虎仙以幣二千、銀酒槍一賂之，令還哈密城印。

translations.literal: Ze thought the tribesmen could be lured with profit; he plotted with Jian and sent Hami Assistant Commander Shayihuxian with two thousand strings of cash and one silver wine-flagon to bribe them, ordering the return of Hami city and seal.
translations.idiomatic: Believing the nomads could be bought off, he and Zhao Jian sent Hami assistant commander Shayihuxian with two thousand strings of coin and a silver wine ewer as a bribe, demanding Hami’s city and seal in return.

sentences.zh: 未得報，輒奏事平，乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Before any reply arrived, he memorialized that affairs were settled and requested retirement on grounds of infirmity.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for a reply he reported victory and asked to retire on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 召還理院事。

translations.literal: He was recalled to handle the ministry’s business.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled him to resume duties at the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史馮時雍言城未歸，澤不宜遽召。

translations.literal: Touring Investigating Censor Feng Shiyong said the city had not been recovered and Ze ought not be summoned back so hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Feng Shiyong protested that Hami was still lost and Peng Ze should not be recalled prematurely.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 初，兵部缺尚書，廷臣共推澤，而王瓊得之，且陰阻澤。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Ministry of War lacked a minister, the court officials together had pushed Ze, but Wang Qiong obtained the post and secretly obstructed Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the war ministry fell vacant, the court had favored Peng Ze, but Wang Qiong won the appointment and quietly worked against him.

sentences.zh: 言官多劾瓊者，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Censorial officials had often impeached Qiong, and from this there was a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Censors had repeatedly attacked Wang Qiong, and bad blood opened between the two men.

sentences.zh: 澤又使酒常淩瓊，瓊愈欲傾之。

translations.literal: Ze also drank heavily and often insulted Qiong, and Qiong all the more wished to overturn him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze drank hard and habitually humiliated Wang Qiong, who grew only more determined to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 澤時時罵錢寧，瓊以語寧，寧未信。

translations.literal: Ze often cursed Qian Ning; Qiong told Ning, but Ning did not yet believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze regularly denounced Qian Ning; Wang Qiong relayed the abuse, but Ning would not credit it.

sentences.zh: 瓊乃邀澤飲，匿寧所親屏間，挑澤醉罵使聞之，寧果大怒。

translations.literal: Qiong then invited Ze to drink, hid one of Ning’s intimates behind a screen, and goaded Ze into drunken cursing so it would be heard; Ning indeed flew into a rage.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong invited Peng Ze to a banquet, hid one of Ning’s confidants behind a screen, and provoked him into drunken abuse within earshot—Qian Ning was finally enraged.

sentences.zh: 會寇大入宣府，廷議以許泰將兵，澤總制東西兩邊軍務。

translations.literal: At that time the enemy made a major incursion into Xuanfu; the court deliberated on having Xu Tai lead troops, with Ze to exercise overall command of military affairs on the eastern and western fronts.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders poured into Xuanfu, the court debated putting Xu Tai in the field while Peng Ze coordinated both eastern and western frontiers.

sentences.zh: 及詔下，罷泰不遣，又不命澤總制，獨令提督兩遊擊兵六千人以行，意以困澤。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Tai was dismissed and not sent; Ze was also not ordered to exercise overall command—he alone was told to lead six thousand men of the two mobile corps, the intent being to embarrass Ze.
translations.idiomatic: The final edict kept Xu Tai at home, denied Peng Ze overall command, and sent him only six thousand troops from two mobile detachments—an obvious setup to humiliate him.

sentences.zh: 澤言：「臣文臣，摧鋒陷陣非臣所能獨任。

translations.literal: Ze said, “Your servant is a civil official; charging the van and breaking the enemy line is not something your servant can undertake alone.”
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze protested, “I am a civil minister; I cannot alone bear the work of leading a charge.”

sentences.zh: 」瓊乃奏遣成國公朱輔。

translations.literal: ” Qiong then memorialized dispatch of the Duke of Cheng Zhu Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong then secured an order sending the Duke of Cheng, Zhu Fu, to join him.

sentences.zh: 會寇遁，澤還理院事。

translations.literal: When the enemy fled, Ze returned to handle the ministry’s business.
translations.idiomatic: Once the raiders withdrew, Peng Ze went back to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 寫亦虎仙者，素桀黠。

translations.literal: Shayihuxian was by nature crafty and defiant.
translations.idiomatic: Shayihuxian had always been cunning and unruly.

sentences.zh: 雖居肅州，陰通土魯番酋速檀滿速兒，為之耳目，據城奪印皆其謀。

translations.literal: Although he dwelt at Suzhou, he secretly communicated with the Turpan chief Sultan Mansur, serving as his eyes and ears; seizing the city and stealing the seal were both his schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Though stationed at Suzhou, he secretly served Turpan’s chief Sultan Mansur as spy and architect of the seizure of Hami and its seal.

sentences.zh: 澤初不知而遣之。

translations.literal: Ze at first did not know this and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze, unaware, had sent him on the mission.

sentences.zh: 滿速兒以城印來歸，留速檀拜牙郎如故。

translations.literal: Mansur returned the city and seal but kept Sultan Bayandorji as before.
translations.idiomatic: Mansur handed back the city and seal yet retained Sultan Bayandorji under his control.

sentences.zh: 虎仙復啖使入寇，曰：「肅州可得也。

translations.literal: Huxian again tempted them to invade, saying, “Suzhou can be taken.”
translations.idiomatic: Shayihuxian once more urged invasion, promising, “Suzhou can be yours.”

sentences.zh: 」滿速兒悅，使其婿馬黑木隨入貢，以覘虛實，且征賄。

translations.literal: ” Mansur was pleased and sent his son-in-law Ma Heimu to enter tribute, to spy out strengths and weaknesses and also to demand bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Mansur sent his son-in-law Ma Heimu with a tribute mission to probe Ming defenses and extort gifts.

sentences.zh: 澤已還，鑒亦遷去，李昆代巡撫，慮他變，質其使於甘州，而驅虎仙出關。

translations.literal: Ze had already returned, and Jian had also been transferred; Li Kun replaced him as grand coordinator. Fearing other changes, he detained their envoy at Ganzhou and drove Huxian beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze was gone and Zhao Jian transferred; Li Kun became grand coordinator, detained the envoys at Ganzhou for fear of treachery, and expelled Shayihuxian beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 虎仙懼弗去。

translations.literal: Huxian feared and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shayihuxian panicked and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 滿速兒聞之怒，復取哈密，分兵據沙州，自率萬騎寇嘉峪關。

translations.literal: When Mansur heard this he was enraged; he again seized Hami, divided troops to hold Shazhou, and himself led ten thousand horsemen to raid Jiayu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Mansur flew into a rage, retook Hami, occupied Shazhou with a detachment, and led ten thousand horsemen against Jiayu Pass.

sentences.zh: 遊擊芮寧與參將蔣存禮禦之。

translations.literal: Mobile-corps commander Rui Ning and Assistant Commander Jiang Cunli resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile-corps commander Rui Ning and assistant commander Jiang Cunli met the invasion.

sentences.zh: 寧以七百人先遇寇沙子壩。

translations.literal: Ning with seven hundred men first encountered the enemy at Shaziba.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Ning with seven hundred men met the vanguard first at Shaziba.

sentences.zh: 寇圍寧，而分兵綴存禮軍。

translations.literal: The enemy surrounded Ning while detaching troops to hold Jiang Cunli’s army in check.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders encircled Rui Ning and pinned Jiang Cunli with a separate force.

sentences.zh: 寧軍盡沒，遂墮城堡，縱殺掠。

translations.literal: Ning’s army was entirely destroyed; the enemy then breached the fortress and slaughtered and plundered at will.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Ning’s detachment was wiped out; the enemy stormed the fortifications and ravaged the countryside.

sentences.zh: 詔澤提督三邊軍務往禦。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ze to supervise military affairs on the three frontiers and go to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Peng Ze to take command of the three frontiers and march to repel them.

sentences.zh: 會副使陳九疇系其使失拜煙答及虎仙等，內應絕，乃復求和。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Commissioner Chen Jiuchou arrested their envoy Ibakiyata together with Huxian and others; with internal collusion cut off, they again sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile vice commissioner Chen Jiuchou seized Ibakiyata and Shayihuxian; cut off from inside help, Turpan sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 澤兵遂罷。

translations.literal: Ze’s troops were then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze’s expedition was stood down.

sentences.zh: 尋乞骸骨歸，馳驛給夫廩如制。

translations.literal: Soon he requested retirement on grounds of infirmity and returned home; courier stations and porters’ grain were supplied by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired home on grounds of age, traveling by imperial courier relay with the usual porter rations.

sentences.zh: 澤既去，瓊追論嘉峪之敗，請窮詰增幣者主名。

translations.literal: After Ze had gone, Qiong pursued the argument over the Jiayu defeat and asked that the persons responsible for increasing the tribute be thoroughly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Once Peng Ze was gone, Wang Qiong reopened the Jiayu disaster and demanded a full inquiry into who had authorized the extra tribute.

sentences.zh: 錢寧從中下其事，大學士梁儲等持之，乃已。

translations.literal: Qian Ning had the matter pushed from within; Grand Secretary Liang Chu and others resisted it, and it was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ning tried to drive the investigation from within, but Grand Secretary Liang Chu and others blocked it until the affair died.

sentences.zh: 會失拜煙答子訟父冤，下法司議，釋寫亦虎仙等。

translations.literal: When Ibakiyata’s son sued over his father’s wrong, the case went to the judicial offices for deliberation, and Shayihuxian and others were released.
translations.idiomatic: When Ibakiyata’s son petitioned over his father’s death, the judiciary reviewed the case and freed Shayihuxian and his party.

sentences.zh: 瓊因請遣給事御史勘失事狀，還報無所引。

translations.literal: Qiong then asked that a supervising secretary and censor be sent to investigate the failure; on their return they reported nothing that could be cited.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong sent a supervising secretary and a censor to investigate the defeat; their report cited no one.

sentences.zh: 瓊遂劾澤妄增金幣，遺書議和，失信啟釁，辱國喪師；

translations.literal: Qiong then impeached Ze for recklessly increasing gold and goods, sending letters to negotiate peace, breaking faith and provoking strife, disgracing the state and losing armies;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong then impeached Peng Ze for lavishing gold, negotiating by private letter, breaking faith, inviting attack, and bringing national shame and military disaster;

sentences.zh: 昆、九疇俱宜罪。

translations.literal: Kun and Jiuchou alike deserved punishment.
translations.idiomatic: he argued that Li Kun and Chen Jiuchou should be punished as well.

sentences.zh: 詔斥澤為民，昆、九疇逮訊。

translations.literal: An edict degraded Ze to commoner status, and Kun and Jiuchou were arrested for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Peng Ze of rank and ordered Li Kun and Chen Jiuchou taken for questioning.

sentences.zh: 昆謫官，九疇除名。

translations.literal: Kun was demoted in office; Jiuchou was removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kun was demoted; Chen Jiuchou was dismissed from service.

sentences.zh: 世宗入繼，錢寧敗，瓊亦得罪。

translations.literal: When the Shizong emperor succeeded, Qian Ning fell, and Qiong also was found guilty.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiajing emperor took the throne, Qian Ning was ruined and Wang Qiong fell with him.

sentences.zh: 御史楊秉中請召澤，遂即家起兵部尚書、太子太保。

translations.literal: Censor Yang Bingzhong asked that Ze be summoned; he was then raised from home to Minister of War and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Bingzhong urged Peng Ze’s recall; he was summoned straight from retirement as Minister of War and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 昆、九疇亦復官。

translations.literal: Kun and Jiuchou also had their offices restored.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kun and Chen Jiuchou were reinstated as well.

sentences.zh: 部事積壞久，澤核功罪，杜幹請，兵政一新。

translations.literal: Ministry business had long been decayed; Ze assessed merit and guilt, stopped improper solicitations, and military administration was made new.
translations.idiomatic: Years of rot had crippled the ministry; Peng Ze judged rewards and blame, shut down backdoor pleading, and renewed military administration.

sentences.zh: 初，正德時，廷臣建白戎務奉俞旨者，多廢格。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Zhengde era, when court officials memorialized on military affairs and received imperial approval, much was left unimplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, many approved military reforms proposed by the court had never been carried out.

sentences.zh: 澤請臚列成書，次第修舉。

translations.literal: Ze asked that they be listed in full and made into a book, to be implemented in order.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze asked that they be compiled into a book and enforced step by step.

sentences.zh: 又請敕九邊守臣，策防禦方略，毋畫境自保。

translations.literal: He also asked that the nine frontier commanders be ordered to devise defense plans and not confine themselves within their own borders for self-protection.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the nine frontier governors to draft coordinated defense plans instead of hoarding troops within their own jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 鎮、巡居中調度，毋相牽制。

translations.literal: Regional commanders and grand coordinators should direct from the center and not restrain one another.
translations.idiomatic: Regional and coordinating officers should orchestrate operations centrally rather than trip one another up.

sentences.zh: 諸邊各以農隙築墻浚濠，修墩臺，飭屯堡，為經久計。

translations.literal: Each frontier should use the farming slack season to build walls, deepen moats, repair beacon towers, and put garrison forts in order, as a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: Every border sector should use the farming off-season to build walls, dig moats, repair beacon towers, and tighten garrison forts as a lasting program.

sentences.zh: 內地盜甫息，敕守臣練卒伍，立保甲，懲匿盜不舉者。

translations.literal: Banditry in the interior had just subsided; he ordered defending officials to drill troops, establish the baojia system, and punish those who concealed bandits and did not report them.
translations.idiomatic: With inland banditry only just quieting, he ordered local defenders to drill militia, institute baojia mutual surveillance, and punish those who hid thieves.

sentences.zh: 且撫西南諸苗蠻，申海禁，汰京軍老弱。

translations.literal: He also pacified the various Miao tribes of the southwest, tightened the maritime prohibition, and weeded out the old and weak among capital troops.
translations.idiomatic: He further pacified southwestern Miao peoples, reinforced the maritime ban, and culled aged and unfit soldiers from the capital armies.

sentences.zh: 帝鹹嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of these in praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and adopted every proposal.

sentences.zh: 詔遣中官楊金、鄭斌、安川更代鎮守，復令張弼、劉瑤守涼州、居庸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered eunuchs Yang Jin, Zheng Bin, and An Chuan to replace the frontier garrison commanders in turn, and again ordered Zhang Bi and Liu Yao to guard Liangzhou and Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched eunuchs Yang Jin, Zheng Bin, and An Chuan to rotate frontier garrison commands and reappointed Zhang Bi and Liu Yao to Liangzhou and Juyong.

sentences.zh: 澤持不可，罷弗遣。

translations.literal: Ze held that this could not be done and stopped the dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze objected and blocked the appointments.

sentences.zh: 四川巡撫胡世寧劾分守中官趙欽，澤因請盡罷諸鎮守。

translations.literal: Sichuan grand coordinator Hu Shining impeached the eunuch Zhao Qin who shared command; Ze therefore asked that all frontier garrison eunuchs be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan grand coordinator Hu Shining attacked the garrison eunuch Zhao Qin, Peng Ze seized the moment to demand abolition of all frontier eunuch commands.

sentences.zh: 時雖不從，其後鎮守竟罷。

translations.literal: At the time the court did not follow this, but afterward the garrison eunuchs were indeed abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused at first, yet in time the garrison eunuchs were abolished after all.

sentences.zh: 在部多所執持。

translations.literal: While at the ministry he often held firm on matters.
translations.idiomatic: As minister he frequently stood his ground on policy.

sentences.zh: 會御史史道以訐楊廷和下獄，澤復劾道。

translations.literal: At that time the censor Shi Dao was imprisoned for denouncing Yang Tinghe, and Ze again impeached Dao.
translations.idiomatic: When censor Shi Dao was thrown into prison for denouncing Yang Tinghe, Peng Ze impeached him again.

sentences.zh: 帝因諭言官，惟大奸及機密事專疏奏，余只具公疏，毋挾私中傷善類。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore instructed the remonstrating officials that only great traitors and confidential matters were to be reported in separate memorials; the rest should be submitted only in joint public memorials, and they must not use private grievances to slander good men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then admonished the censorate that only grave treason and confidential matters warranted individual memorials; everything else belonged in collective submissions, and officials must not settle private scores by smearing upright colleagues.

sentences.zh: 詔下，給事御史交章劾澤阻言路，壞祖宗法。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, supervising secretaries and censors submitted memorial after memorial impeaching Ze for obstructing the remonstrance channels and violating ancestral law.
translations.idiomatic: Once the edict appeared, supervising secretaries and censors flooded the throne with charges that Peng Ze had blocked the remonstrance channels and broken ancestral precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝乃從吏部言，停前諭。

translations.literal: The emperor then followed the Ministry of Personnel's advice and suspended the earlier instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then heeded the Ministry of Personnel and revoked the earlier directive.

sentences.zh: 澤不自安，累疏乞休。

translations.literal: Ze no longer felt secure in office and repeatedly memorialized asking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his post, Peng Ze memorialized again and again requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 言者復交劾之，乃加少保，賜敕乘傳歸。

translations.literal: The remonstrators again submitted joint impeachments against him, whereupon he was promoted to Junior Guardian and granted an imperial letter allowing him to return home by official relay.
translations.idiomatic: When critics renewed their attacks, the court made him Junior Guardian and sent him home with an imperial letter and relay horses.

sentences.zh: 錦衣百戶王邦奇憾澤嘗抑己，上書言哈密失國，由澤賂番求和所致，語侵楊廷和、陳九疇等。

translations.literal: Wang Bangqi, a hundred-household officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, resented that Ze had once restrained him and submitted a memorial saying that the loss of Hami had been caused by Ze's bribing the tribes to seek peace, with language that also implicated Yang Tinghe, Chen Jiuchou, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bangqi, a hundred-household officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, still smarting from Peng Ze's earlier rebuke, memorialized that Hami had been lost because Ze had bribed the tribes into a peace settlement, and his charges also touched Yang Tinghe, Chen Jiuchou, and others.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼方疾廷和，遂逮九疇廷訊，戍邊。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and Gui E, who were then hostile to Tinghe, had Jiuchou arrested and interrogated at court, and he was banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E, then eager to strike at Yang Tinghe's circle, had Chen Jiuchou seized for court interrogation and exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 澤復奪官為民，家居郁郁以卒。

translations.literal: Ze was again stripped of office and reduced to commoner status; he lived at home in gloom until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze was stripped of rank once more and reduced to commoner status; he lived out his days at home in dejection until death.

sentences.zh: 總制尚書唐龍言：「澤孝友廉直，先後討平群盜，功在盟府。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Minister Tang Long said: "Ze was filial, fraternal, incorrupt, and upright; he successively suppressed bandit groups, and his achievements are recorded in the Hall of Fealty."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Minister Tang Long wrote: "Peng Ze was filial, loyal to friends, upright, and incorruptible; he put down bandit armies one after another, and his deeds belong in the Hall of Fealty."

sentences.zh: 陛下起之田間，俾掌邦政。

translations.literal: Your Majesty raised him from the fields and had him administer the state's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty plucked him from private life and entrusted him with the governance of the realm.

sentences.zh: 澤孜孜奉國，復為讒言構罷。

translations.literal: Ze served the state tirelessly, yet was again driven from office by slander.
translations.idiomatic: He served the state tirelessly, only to be driven out again by malicious accusations.

sentences.zh: 今歿已五年，所遺二妾，衣食不給。

translations.literal: It is now five years since his death, and the two concubines he left behind cannot supply themselves with food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Five years after his death, the two concubines he left behind still cannot afford food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 請核澤往勞，復官加恤，以作忠臣之氣。

translations.literal: I ask that Ze's past labors be verified, his office restored, and additional posthumous honors granted, so as to uphold the spirit of loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that his past service be reviewed, his rank restored, and additional honors granted, so as to sustain the morale of loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: The request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官，謚襄毅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Longqing reign his office was restored and he was given the posthumous title Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign his rank was restored and he was posthumously titled Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 毛伯溫，字汝厲，吉水人。

translations.literal: Mao Bowen, styled Ruli, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bowen, courtesy name Ruli, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 祖超，廣西知府。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chao was prefect of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chao had served as prefect of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 伯溫登正德三年進士，授紹興府推官。

translations.literal: Bowen passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Zhengde reign and was appointed investigating magistrate of Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde year 3 and was appointed investigating magistrate of Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，巡按福建、河南。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor and conducted inspection tours in Fujian and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor, he toured Fujian and Henan on inspection duty.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，中官張銳、張忠等論死，其黨蕭敬、韋霦陰緩之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, the eunuchs Zhang Rui, Zhang Zhong, and others were sentenced to death, but their partisans Xiao Jing and Wei Rong secretly sought to delay execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, the eunuchs Zhang Rui and Zhang Zhong were condemned to death, but their allies Xiao Jing and Wei Rong worked behind the scenes to stall the sentences.

sentences.zh: 伯溫請並誅敬、霦，中官為屏氣。

translations.literal: Bowen asked that Jing and Rong also be executed, and the eunuchs held their breath in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen demanded that Jing and Rong be executed as well, and the eunuch faction fell silent in fear.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，遷大理寺丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he was transferred to be vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he was transferred to the Court of Judicial Review as vice director.

sentences.zh: 擢右僉都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, he was sent to govern Ningxia as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 李福達獄起，坐為大理時失入，褫職歸。

translations.literal: When the Li Fuda case arose, he was punished for a wrongful judgment while at the Court of Judicial Review, stripped of office, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Li Fuda case erupted, he was blamed for a wrongful ruling from his days at the Court of Judicial Review, stripped of office, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 用薦起故官，撫山西，移順天，皆未赴。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was restored to his former office and appointed to govern Shanxi, then transferred to Shuntian, but he went to neither post.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended back to office, he was assigned to govern Shanxi and then Shuntian, but he never took either post.

sentences.zh: 改理院事，進左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to handle affairs at the Court of Judicial Review and promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to the Court of Judicial Review and promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 為趙府宗人祐椋所訐，解官候勘。

translations.literal: He was denounced by You Liang, a clansman of the Zhao princely establishment, and was removed from office pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: You Liang, a clansman of the Zhao princely establishment, denounced him, and he was suspended pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 已，復褫職。

translations.literal: Afterward he was again stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually stripped of rank once more.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，皇嗣生，將頒詔外國。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year a royal heir was born, and an edict was to be promulgated to foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year 15 a royal heir was born, and the court prepared to announce the birth to foreign states.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書夏言以安南久失朝貢，不當遣使，請討之。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xia Yan argued that because Annam had long failed to send tribute, no envoy should be dispatched there and requested a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Xia Yan argued that Annam had long ceased tribute missions and should not receive an envoy; he urged a punitive expedition instead.

sentences.zh: 遂起伯溫右都御史，與鹹寧侯仇鸞治兵待命。

translations.literal: Bowen was then recalled as Right Censor-in-Chief and, together with Marquis Qiu Luan of Xianning, prepared troops and awaited orders.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen was recalled as Right Censor-in-Chief and, with Marquis Qiu Luan of Xianning, began mobilizing troops for action.

sentences.zh: 以父喪辭，不許。

translations.literal: He declined on grounds of mourning for his father, but permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to withdraw for his father's mourning, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 明年五月至京，上方略六事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year he reached the capital and presented six strategic proposals to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The following May he reached the capital and submitted six strategic proposals to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會安南世孫黎寧遣陪臣鄭惟僚等訴莫登庸弒逆，請興師復仇。

translations.literal: At that time Li Ning, the hereditary grandson of Annam, sent attendant ministers such as Zheng Weiliao to complain that Mac Dang Dung had committed regicide and to request that troops be raised for revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Li Ning, Annam's hereditary heir, sent attendant ministers including Zheng Weiliao to accuse Mac Dang Dung of regicide and plead for a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝疑其不實，命暫緩師，敕兩廣、雲南守臣勘報，而命伯溫協理院事。

translations.literal: The emperor doubted the truth of the claim, ordered the campaign temporarily halted, instructed the defending officials of the Two Guangs and Yunnan to investigate and report, and ordered Bowen to assist in handling Court of Judicial Review affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted the account, suspended the campaign, ordered officials in the Two Guangs and Yunnan to investigate, and had Bowen assist at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 御史何維柏請聽伯溫終制，不許。

translations.literal: Censor He Weibai asked that Bowen be allowed to complete his mourning period, but permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Censor He Weibai asked that Bowen be allowed to finish mourning, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 伯溫引疾不出，至禫除始起視事。

translations.literal: Bowen pleaded illness and did not take up duties until the end of mourning, when he finally resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen stayed away on grounds of illness and did not resume duty until mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 其冬遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，黔國公沐朝輔等以登庸降表至，請宥罪許貢。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year, Duke Mu Zhaofu of Qian and others arrived with Dang Dung's surrender memorial, asking that his crimes be pardoned and tribute allowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 17, Duke Mu Zhaofu of Qian and others arrived with Mac Dang Dung's surrender memorial, asking pardon and permission to resume tribute.

sentences.zh: 先是，雲南巡撫汪文盛奏登庸聞發兵進討，遣使潛覘。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yunnan grand coordinator Wang Wensheng had memorialized that when Dang Dung heard troops were being sent against him, he dispatched envoys to spy secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yunnan grand coordinator Wang Wensheng reported that once Mac Dang Dung heard of the planned expedition, he sent spies to reconnoiter.

sentences.zh: 帝已敕遵前詔進兵，文盛又納安南降人武文淵策，具言登庸可破狀，復傳檄安南令奉表獻地。

translations.literal: The emperor had already ordered that the earlier edict be followed and troops advance; Wensheng also accepted the plan of the Annamese defector Wu Wenyuan, fully describing how Dang Dung could be defeated, and again issued a proclamation to Annam ordering submission of a memorial and cession of territory.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already ordered troops forward under the earlier edict; Wang Wensheng also took counsel from the Annamese defector Wu Wenyuan, laid out a plan to break Mac Dang Dung, and again demanded submission and territorial surrender.

sentences.zh: 及是，下朝輔奏付廷議，僉言不可許。

translations.literal: At this point Zhaofu's memorial was submitted to court deliberation, and all said it could not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaofu's memorial reached court, the consensus was that surrender could not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 乃改伯溫兵部尚書兼右都御史，克期啟行。

translations.literal: Bowen was then changed to Minister of War concurrently serving as Right Censor-in-Chief, with a fixed date set for departure.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen was then made Minister of War and concurrent Right Censor-in-Chief, with a fixed departure date.

sentences.zh: 帝以用兵事重，無必討意，特欲威服之。

translations.literal: Because the matter of using troops was weighty, the emperor had no fixed intention to punish them and only wished to overawe them into submission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated war as a grave matter and had no fixed appetite for conquest; he mainly wanted to intimidate Annam into submission.

sentences.zh: 而兵部尚書張瓚無所畫，視帝意為可否。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Zan, however, had no plan of his own and judged what was permissible by the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Zan offered no plan of his own and simply mirrored the emperor's mood.

sentences.zh: 朝論多主不當興師，顧不敢顯諫。

translations.literal: Court opinion mostly held that troops should not be raised, yet no one dared remonstrate openly.
translations.idiomatic: Most at court believed war was unwise, yet few dared say so openly.

sentences.zh: 制下數月，兩廣總督侍郎張經以用兵方略上，且言須兵三十萬，餉百六十萬石。

translations.literal: Several months after the order was issued, Vice Minister Zhang Jing, grand coordinator of the Two Guangs, submitted a military plan and said that three hundred thousand troops and 1.6 million shi of provisions would be required.
translations.idiomatic: Months after the order, Two Guangs grand coordinator Vice Minister Zhang Jing submitted a war plan calling for three hundred thousand troops and 1.6 million shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 欽州知州林希元則極言登庸易取，請即日出師。

translations.literal: Lin Xiyuan, prefect of Qinzhou, on the other hand strongly argued that Dang Dung could easily be taken and asked that troops march out that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou prefect Lin Xiyuan insisted Mac Dang Dung would be easy to defeat and urged immediate mobilization.

sentences.zh: 瓚不敢決，復請廷議。

translations.literal: Zan did not dare decide and again requested court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zan would not decide and sent the question back to court.

sentences.zh: 議上無成策，帝不懌，讓瓚，師復止。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted there was no settled plan; the emperor was displeased, rebuked Zan, and the campaign was halted again.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation produced no clear plan; the emperor was displeased, rebuked Zhang Zan, and halted the campaign again.

sentences.zh: 命伯溫仍協理院事。

translations.literal: Bowen was ordered to continue assisting in Court of Judicial Review affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen was ordered back to assisting at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，帝幸承天。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year the emperor visited Chengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The following February the emperor traveled to Chengtian.

sentences.zh: 詔伯溫總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Bowen to take overall command of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put Bowen in overall command of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 俄選宮僚，加兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was selected among palace staff and additionally appointed Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was chosen as a palace adviser and additionally made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 大同所轄鎮邊、鎮川、弘賜、鎮河、鎮虜五堡，相距二百餘里，極邊近賊帳。

translations.literal: The five forts of Zhenbian, Zhenchuan, Hongci, Zhenhe, and Zhenlu under Datong's jurisdiction were more than two hundred li apart and lay on the outermost frontier close to the enemy camps.
translations.idiomatic: The five forts under Datong—Zhenbian, Zhenchuan, Hongci, Zhenhe, and Zhenlu—lay more than two hundred li apart on the outer frontier, hard against the enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 自巡撫張文錦以築堡致亂，後無敢議修者。

translations.literal: Ever since grand coordinator Zhang Wenjin had caused unrest by building forts, no one afterward dared discuss repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since grand coordinator Zhang Wenjin's fort-building had sparked rebellion, no one dared propose new construction.

sentences.zh: 伯溫曰：「變所由生，以任用匪人，非建議謬也。

translations.literal: Bowen said: "The disturbance arose because unworthy men were employed, not because the proposal to build was mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: Bowen said: "The trouble came from appointing the wrong men, not from the fort-building plan itself."

sentences.zh: 」卒營之。

translations.literal: In the end he built them.
translations.idiomatic: He went ahead and built them anyway.

sentences.zh: 募軍三千防守，給以閑田，永除其賦。

translations.literal: He recruited three thousand troops for defense, granted them idle land, and permanently exempted them from tax.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited three thousand garrison troops, granted them idle land, and permanently exempted them from tax.

sentences.zh: 邊防賴焉。

translations.literal: The frontier defenses relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier defenses depended on these measures.

sentences.zh: 錄功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His service was rewarded with promotion to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是時登庸懼討，數上表乞降。

translations.literal: At that time Dang Dung, fearing punitive action, repeatedly submitted memorials begging to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: By then Mac Dang Dung, fearing attack, repeatedly petitioned to surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝亦欲因撫之，遣侍郎黃綰招諭。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to pacify him by this means and dispatched Vice Minister Huang Wan to summon and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also hoped to settle the matter peacefully and sent Vice Minister Huang Wan to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 綰多所要求，帝怒，罷綰。

translations.literal: Wan made many demands, the emperor grew angry, and Wan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan drove too hard a bargain; the emperor grew angry and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 再下廷議，鹹言當討，帝從之。

translations.literal: The matter was again submitted to court deliberation; all said he should be punished, and the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The question went back to court, where the consensus favored war, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 閏七月命伯溫、鸞南征。

translations.literal: In the intercalary seventh month Bowen and Luan were ordered on a southern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month Bowen and Qiu Luan were ordered south on campaign.

sentences.zh: 文武三品以下不用命者，許軍令從事。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of third rank and below who disobeyed orders were permitted to be dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials below third rank who disobeyed could be punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 伯溫等至廣西，會總督張經，總兵官安遠侯柳珣，參政翁萬達、張嶽等議，征兩廣、福建、湖廣狼土官兵凡十二萬五千余人，分三哨，自憑祥、龍峒、思陵州入，而以奇兵二為聲援。

translations.literal: When Bowen and the others reached Guangxi, they met with grand coordinator Zhang Jing, regional commander Marquis Liu Xun of Anyuan, and administration commissioners Weng Wanda and Zhang Yue to plan the campaign; they mobilized more than 125,000 Lang and native troops from the Two Guangs, Fujian, and Huguang, divided them into three columns to enter by Pingxiang, Longdong, and Siling Prefecture, and used two detachments of surprise troops as supporting forces.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxi, Bowen met grand coordinator Zhang Jing, regional commander Marquis Liu Xun of Anyuan, and administration commissioners Weng Wanda and Zhang Yue to plan the campaign; they mustered more than 125,000 Lang and native troops from the Two Guangs, Fujian, and Huguang, divided them into three columns entering through Pingxiang, Longdong, and Siling Prefecture, and posted two flanking detachments in support.

sentences.zh: 檄雲南巡撫汪文盛帥兵駐蓮花灘，亦分三道進。

translations.literal: They also issued a dispatch ordering Yunnan grand coordinator Wang Wensheng to lead troops stationed at Lianhua Beach and likewise advance in three routes.
translations.idiomatic: They also ordered Yunnan grand coordinator Wang Wensheng to hold Lianhua Beach and advance in three columns.

sentences.zh: 部署已定，會鸞有罪召還，即以珣代。

translations.literal: Once the deployment was settled, Luan was found guilty and recalled, and Xun was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Once the plan was set, Qiu Luan was recalled for misconduct and Liu Xun replaced him.

sentences.zh: 十九年秋，伯溫等進駐南寧。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the nineteenth year Bowen and the others advanced and encamped at Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of year 19 Bowen and his staff established headquarters at Nanning.

sentences.zh: 檄安南臣民，諭以天朝興滅繼絕之義，罪止登庸父子，舉郡縣降者以其地授之。

translations.literal: They issued a proclamation to the officials and people of Annam, explaining the Heavenly Court's principle of restoring extinguished states and continuing broken lineages; guilt would be limited to Dang Dung and his son, and any prefecture or county that surrendered would have its territory granted to it.
translations.idiomatic: They proclaimed to Annam's officials and people the court's doctrine of restoring fallen states and preserving broken lineages: only Mac Dang Dung and his son would be punished, and any district that surrendered would keep its lands.

sentences.zh: 懸重購購登庸父子，而宣諭登庸籍土地、人民納款，即如詔書宥罪。

translations.literal: They posted a heavy reward for the capture of Dang Dung and his son, while also announcing to Dang Dung that if he registered land and people and submitted, he would be pardoned as the edict promised.
translations.idiomatic: They offered a rich bounty for Mac Dang Dung and his son, while also telling Dang Dung that registering land and people and submitting would bring the pardon promised in the edict.

sentences.zh: 登庸大懼，遣使詣萬達乞降，詞甚哀。

translations.literal: Dang Dung was greatly afraid and sent envoys to Wanda begging to surrender, with words of great lament.
translations.idiomatic: Mac Dang Dung was terrified and sent envoys to Weng Wanda pleading to surrender in the most abject terms.

sentences.zh: 萬達送之伯溫所。

translations.literal: Wanda sent them to Bowen's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda forwarded them to Bowen's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 伯溫承制許之，宣天子恩威，納其圖籍，並所還欽州四峒地。

translations.literal: Bowen, acting on imperial authority, granted the request, proclaimed the Son of Heaven's grace and majesty, accepted their maps and registers, and also received the return of the four dong districts of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on imperial authority, Bowen accepted the surrender, proclaimed the emperor's blend of mercy and force, took their maps and registers, and received back the four dong districts of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 權令還國聽命。

translations.literal: He provisionally ordered them to return to their state and await commands.
translations.idiomatic: He provisionally allowed them to return home and await further orders.

sentences.zh: 馳疏以聞，帝大悅。

translations.literal: He sent an urgent memorial to report this, and the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an urgent report to court, and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 詔改安南國為安南都統使司，以登庸為都統使，世襲，置十三宣撫司，令自署置。

translations.literal: An edict changed the state of Annam into the Annam Regional Military Commission, appointed Dang Dung Regional Commander with hereditary succession, established thirteen pacification commissions, and allowed him to appoint officials himself.
translations.idiomatic: An edict transformed Annam into the Annam Regional Military Commission, made Mac Dang Dung hereditary Regional Commander, established thirteen pacification commissions, and let him appoint his own officials.

sentences.zh: 伯溫受命歲餘，不發一矢，而安南定，由帝本不欲用兵故也。

translations.literal: More than a year after receiving his commission, Bowen had not loosed a single arrow, yet Annam was settled, because the emperor from the outset had not wished to use force.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year into his command, Bowen had not fired a single arrow, yet Annam was pacified—because the emperor had never truly wanted war.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed he was promoted to Senior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to Senior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月還朝，復理院事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year he returned to court and again handled Court of Judicial Review affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 21 he returned to court and resumed work at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 邊關數有警，伯溫請築京師外城。

translations.literal: The frontier repeatedly reported alarms, and Bowen requested construction of an outer wall for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: With repeated frontier alarms, Bowen proposed building an outer wall around the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝已報可，給事中劉養直言，廟工方興，物力難繼，乃命暫止。

translations.literal: The emperor had already approved, but supervising secretary Liu Yangzhi said that temple construction was then underway and material resources could not support both projects, so the order was temporarily halted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already approved, but supervising secretary Liu Yangzhi argued that temple construction was already straining resources, and the project was suspended.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，張瓚卒，伯溫代為兵部。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year Zhang Zan died, and Bowen replaced him as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: That October, when Zhang Zan died, Bowen succeeded him as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 瓚貪黷，在部八年，戎備盡墮。

translations.literal: Zan had been corrupt; during his eight years at the ministry military readiness had completely collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zan had been corrupt, and during his eight years at the ministry frontier readiness had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 伯溫會廷臣議上防邊二十四事，軍令一新。

translations.literal: Bowen convened court officials to deliberate and submit twenty-four frontier defense measures, and military discipline was entirely renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen convened court officials to submit twenty-four frontier reforms, and military discipline was thoroughly renewed.

sentences.zh: 言官建議，請核實新軍、京軍及內府力士、匠役，以裕國儲。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials proposed verifying the rolls of new troops, capital troops, and the strongmen and artisans of the inner palace, so as to enlarge state reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Censors proposed auditing rolls of new troops, capital garrisons, and inner-palace laborers and artisans to ease state finances.

sentences.zh: 伯溫因上冗濫當革者二十余條，凡錦衣、騰驤諸衛，禦馬、內官、尚膳諸監，素為中貴盤踞者，盡在革中。

translations.literal: Bowen thereupon submitted more than twenty items of wasteful excess that should be abolished; all the posts long monopolized by inner eunuchs, including the Embroidered Uniform Guard, Tengxiang Guard, Imperial Horse Office, Inner Palace Office, Imperial Kitchen Office, and other offices, were included in the reforms.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen followed with more than twenty proposed cuts to wasteful posts, targeting eunuch-dominated offices from the Embroidered Uniform and Tengxiang guards to the Imperial Horse, Inner Palace, and Imperial Kitchen directorates.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，立命清汰。

translations.literal: The emperor praised the plan and immediately ordered a purge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and immediately ordered a purge.

sentences.zh: 宿弊頗厘，而左右近習多不悅。

translations.literal: Long-standing abuses were largely corrected, but many of those close to the emperor were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Long-standing abuses were largely corrected, but many of the emperor's intimates were displeased.

sentences.zh: 二十三年秋，順天巡撫朱方以防秋畢請撤客兵。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-third year, Shuntian grand coordinator Zhu Fang, because the autumn defense season had ended, requested withdrawal of guest troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of year 23, Shuntian grand coordinator Zhu Fang asked to withdraw guest troops once the autumn defense season ended.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寇大入，直逼畿輔。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy raided in force and pressed straight toward the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the enemy raided in force and drove toward the capital region.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，並械總督翟鵬遣戍，斃方杖下。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, had both men shackled, banished grand coordinator Zhai Peng to the frontier, and had Fang beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious: grand coordinator Zhai Peng was shackled and exiled, and Zhu Fang was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 御史舒汀言，方止議撤薊兵，而並撤宣、大，則伯溫與職方郎韓最也。

translations.literal: Censor Shu Ting said that Fang had only proposed withdrawing Ji troops, but the simultaneous withdrawal from Xuanfu and Datong had been the doing of Bowen and Bureau of Military Appointments director Han Zui.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shu Ting argued that Zhu Fang had only proposed withdrawing Ji troops, while the broader pullout from Xuanfu and Datong had been ordered by Bowen and Bureau of Military Appointments director Han Zui.

sentences.zh: 帝遂削伯溫籍，杖最八十，戍極邊。

translations.literal: The emperor then struck Bowen from the rolls, had Zui beaten eighty strokes, and banished him to the outermost frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then struck Bowen from the rolls, had Han Zui beaten eighty strokes, and exiled him to the remotest frontier.

sentences.zh: 伯溫歸，疽發背卒。

translations.literal: Bowen returned home, a carbuncle broke out on his back, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen went home, developed a carbuncle on his back, and died.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，復官，賜恤。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Bowen's office was restored and posthumous honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Bowen's rank was restored and posthumous honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚襄懋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the title Xiangmao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was posthumously titled Xiangmao.

sentences.zh: 伯溫氣宇沈毅，飲啖兼十人。

translations.literal: Bowen's bearing was deep and resolute; in eating and drinking he matched ten men.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen had a grave, resolute bearing, and at table he could eat and drink as much as ten men.

sentences.zh: 臨事決機，不動聲色。

translations.literal: When facing affairs he decided strategy without moving voice or countenance.
translations.idiomatic: In handling affairs he made decisions without the slightest change in voice or expression.

sentences.zh: 安南之役，萬達、嶽策為多。

translations.literal: In the Annam campaign, Wanda and Yue Ce contributed the most.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Annam, Weng Wanda and Yue Ce did most of the strategic work.

sentences.zh: 伯溫力薦於朝，二人遂得任用。

translations.literal: Bowen strongly recommended them at court, and the two men were then appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen pressed their case at court, and the two were duly appointed.

sentences.zh: 汪文盛，字希周，崇陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Wensheng, style name Xizhou, was a man of Chongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wensheng, courtesy name Xizhou, was a native of Chongyang.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde year 6.

sentences.zh: 授饒州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 有顧嵩者，挾刃入淮王祐棨府，被執，誣文盛使刺王。

translations.literal: There was a man named Gu Song who, carrying a blade, entered the residence of Prince Huai Youqi, was seized, and falsely accused Wensheng of sending him to assassinate the prince.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Gu Song forced his way, blade in hand, into the residence of Prince Huai Youqi, was seized, and falsely claimed Wensheng had sent him to assassinate the prince.

sentences.zh: 下獄訊治，久之得白，還官。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned and interrogated; after a long time his innocence was established, and he resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned and tried; after a long time he was cleared and restored to his post.

sentences.zh: 事詳《淮王傳》。

translations.literal: The matter is detailed in the Biography of Prince Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recounted in full in the Biography of Prince Huai.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部主事，偕同官諫武宗南巡，杖闕下。

translations.literal: He entered service as a secretary in the Ministry of War; together with fellow officials he remonstrated against Emperor Wuzong's southern tour and was beaten below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of War as a secretary and, with fellow officials, remonstrated against Emperor Wuzong's southern tour, for which he was beaten at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，歷福州知府，遷浙江、陜西副使，皆督學校。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he served in succession as prefect of Fuzhou and was promoted to vice commissioner in Zhejiang and Shaanxi, in each case supervising schools.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he served as prefect of Fuzhou, then as educational commissioner in Zhejiang and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 擢雲南按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，廷議將討安南。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year the court deliberated on dispatching a campaign against Annam.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year 15 the court began planning a punitive expedition against Annam.

sentences.zh: 以文盛才，就拜右僉都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: Because of Wensheng's ability, he was immediately appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: On account of Wensheng's talent he was immediately made Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of the region.

sentences.zh: 黔國公沐朝輔幼，兵事一決於文盛。

translations.literal: Duke Mu Zhaofu of Qian was young; military affairs were decided entirely by Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu Zhaofu of Qian was still young, and all military decisions fell to Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 副使鮑象賢言剿不如撫，文盛然之。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Bao Xiangxian said that suppression was inferior to pacification; Wensheng agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Bao Xiangxian argued that pacification was preferable to extermination, and Wensheng agreed.

sentences.zh: 會聞莫登庸已篡位，安南舊臣不服，多據地構兵。

translations.literal: It happened that word came Mac Dang Dung had usurped the throne; old ministers of Annam would not submit, and many held territory and raised arms.
translations.idiomatic: Word then arrived that Mac Dang Dung had seized the throne; former Annamese ministers refused to submit, and many held territory and took up arms.

sentences.zh: 有武文淵者，據宣光，以所部萬人降。

translations.literal: There was Wu Wenyuan, who held Xuanguang and surrendered with ten thousand men under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wenyuan held Xuanguang and surrendered with the ten thousand men under his command.

sentences.zh: 獻進兵地圖，且言舊臣阮仁蓮、黎景眉等皆分據一方與登庸抗，天兵至，號召國中義士，諸方並起，登庸可擒也。

translations.literal: He presented a campaign map and further said that former ministers Ruan Renlian, Li Jingmei, and others each held a region in resistance to Dang Dung; when the Heavenly Army arrived, if they called forth righteous men throughout the country and all regions rose together, Dang Dung could be captured.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a campaign map and reported that former ministers Ruan Renlian, Li Jingmei, and others each held territory in defiance of Mac Dang Dung; once the imperial army arrived and rallied loyalists across the realm, every region would rise together and Dang Dung could be taken.
