sentences.zh: 文盛以聞。

translations.literal: Wensheng reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 授文淵四品章服，子弟給冠帶。

translations.literal: Wu Wenyuan was granted fourth-rank insignia and robes; his sons and younger relatives were given official caps and belts.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan was granted fourth-rank insignia and robes, and his sons and younger kinsmen received official caps and belts.

sentences.zh: 文盛又招安南旁近諸國助討，皆聽命。

translations.literal: Wensheng also recruited neighboring states around Annam to assist in the punitive expedition, and all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng also rallied neighboring states around Annam to join the expedition, and all complied.

sentences.zh: 乃奏言：「老撾地廣兵眾，可使當一面。

translations.literal: He then memorialized, saying: "Laos is broad in territory and numerous in troops; it can be made to hold one front.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized: "Laos is broad in territory and strong in manpower; it can be assigned to hold one front.

sentences.zh: 八百、車裏、孟艮多兵象，可備征調。

translations.literal: Bamo, Cheli, and Menggen have many troops and elephants and can serve for mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: Bamo, Cheli, and Menggen have ample troops and war elephants and can be mobilized as needed.

sentences.zh: 酋長俱未襲職，乞免其保勘，先授以官，彼必鼓勇為用。

translations.literal: Their chieftains have all not yet inherited office; I beg that their guarantor investigations be waived and offices granted first—they will surely rouse courage and serve."
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftains have not yet formally inherited office; I ask that guarantee investigations be waived and appointments made at once—they will then serve with full zeal."

sentences.zh: 」帝悉從之。

translations.literal: The emperor fully approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved everything.

sentences.zh: 文盛乃檄安南所部以土地歸者，仍故職，並諭登庸歸命。

translations.literal: Wensheng then issued a dispatch that those in Annam who returned land would keep their former posts, and also ordered Dang Dung to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng issued a proclamation promising former ranks to Annamese commanders who returned territory, and summoned Mac Dang Dung to submit.

sentences.zh: 攻破鎮守營，方瀛救之失利。

translations.literal: They broke through the garrison camp; Fang Ying went to rescue but was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They overran the garrison camp; Fang Ying led a relief force but was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 登庸部眾多來附，文盛列營樹柵蓮花灘處之。

translations.literal: Many of Dang Dung's followers came over; Wensheng set up camps and palisades at Lianhua Beach to accommodate them.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Dang Dung's followers defected, and Wensheng encamped them at Lianhua Beach behind palisades.

sentences.zh: 蓮花灘者，蒙自縣地，當交、廣水陸沖，為安南腹裏。

translations.literal: Lianhua Beach was territory of Mengzi County, at the land-and-water crossroads of Jiaozhi and Guangxi, the heartland of Annam.
translations.idiomatic: Lianhua Beach lay in Mengzi County, at the land and river junction between Jiaozhi and Guangxi—the heartland of Annam.

sentences.zh: 登庸益懼，請降，願修貢，因言黎寧阮氏子，所持印亦偽。

translations.literal: Dang Dung grew more fearful, requested surrender, and wished to resume tribute; he further said that Li Ning, son of the Nguyen house, and the seal he held were also false.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Dung grew alarmed, asked to surrender, offered to resume tribute, and claimed that Li Ning of the Nguyen house and the seal he bore were likewise spurious.

sentences.zh: 文盛以聞，朝議不許。

translations.literal: Wensheng reported it; court deliberation did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng reported this, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 既而毛伯溫至南寧，受登庸降如文盛議，安南遂定。

translations.literal: Before long Mao Bowen arrived at Nanning, accepted Dang Dung's surrender as Wensheng had proposed, and Annam was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Mao Bowen reached Nanning, accepted Dang Dung's surrender as Wensheng had urged, and Annam was pacified.

sentences.zh: 是役也，功成於伯溫，然伐謀制勝，文盛功為多。

translations.literal: In this campaign, success was credited to Bowen, yet in planning victory through strategy Wensheng's merit was greater.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign the final success went to Bowen, but Wensheng contributed most to the strategic planning that won the war.

sentences.zh: 及論功，伯溫及兩廣鎮巡官俱進秩，而文盛止賚銀幣。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed, Bowen and the military and surveillance officials of the Two Guangs all received rank advancement, while Wensheng received only silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were dispensed, Bowen and the Two Guangs commanders all gained promotions, while Wensheng received only silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 奸人唐弼請開大理銀礦，帝許之。

translations.literal: A schemer named Tang Bi asked to open silver mines in Dali; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: A schemer named Tang Bi petitioned to open silver mines in Dali, and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 文盛斥其妄，下之吏。

translations.literal: Wensheng denounced his falsity and handed him over to the magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng denounced the scheme as spurious and had him handed over to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 召為大理卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned as chief minister of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as chief minister of Dali.

sentences.zh: 九廟災，道病，自陳疏少緩，令致仕。

translations.literal: When disaster struck the Nine Temples he fell ill on the road; in a self-accusation memorial he was somewhat slow, and was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: After fire devastated the Nine Temples he fell ill en route; a tardy memorial of self-accusation led to an order of retirement.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜恤如制。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous condolence was granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and posthumous honors were granted as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 從子宗伊，字子衡，為文盛後。

translations.literal: His nephew Zongyi, style name Ziheng, became Wensheng's heir.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zongyi, courtesy name Ziheng, was made Wensheng's heir.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the seventeenth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiajing year 17.

sentences.zh: 除浮梁知縣，累官兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Fuliang and rose through posts to become a director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Fuliang and rose to become a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 楊繼盛劾嚴嵩及其孫鵠冒功事，宗伊議不撓。

translations.literal: When Yang Jisheng impeached Yan Song and his grandson Hu for falsely claiming merit, Zongyi's deliberation did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jisheng impeached Yan Song and his grandson Yan Hu for falsely claiming merit, Zongyi would not bend in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 忤嵩，自免歸。

translations.literal: He offended Song and resigned to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Song and resigned to go home.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，起南京吏部郎中，歷應天府尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was recalled as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel and served in succession as prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he was recalled as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel and later served as prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 裁諸司供億，歲省民財萬計。

translations.literal: He cut the provision costs of the various offices, saving the people's wealth by tens of thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: He slashed departmental supply costs, saving tens of thousands in public funds each year.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，進南京大理卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was promoted to chief minister of Dali at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he was promoted to chief minister of Dali at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 三遷戶部尚書總督倉場，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Minister of Revenue and overseer of the granaries, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After three further promotions he became Minister of Revenue and superintendent of the grain depots, then retired and died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚恭惠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the title Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was posthumously titled Gonghui.

sentences.zh: 鮑象賢，歙人。

translations.literal: Bao Xiangxian was a man of She County.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xiangxian was a native of She County.

sentences.zh: 由進士授御史，歷雲南副使。

translations.literal: Through the jinshi degree he was appointed censor and served in succession as vice commissioner in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi, he became a censor and later served as vice commissioner in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 毛伯溫檄文盛會師，以象賢領中哨。

translations.literal: Mao Bowen dispatched Wensheng to join forces and placed Xiangxian in command of the central division.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bowen ordered Wang Wensheng to link up and put Xiangxian in command of the center column.

sentences.zh: 屢遷右副都御史，巡撫陜西，代石簡撫雲南。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he became Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, grand coordinator of Shaanxi, and replaced Shi Jian in governing Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, served as grand coordinator of Shaanxi, and replaced Shi Jian as Yunnan governor.

sentences.zh: 初，元江土舍那鑒殺知府那憲以叛，布政使徐樾往招降被殺。

translations.literal: At first the native clerk Na Jian of Yuanjiang killed Prefect Na Xian in rebellion; Administrative Commissioner Xu Yue went to summon surrender and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Yuanjiang native chieftain Na Jian murdered Prefect Na Xian in rebellion; Administrative Commissioner Xu Yue went to negotiate surrender and was killed.

sentences.zh: 簡攻之未克，坐樾事罷，而象賢代之。

translations.literal: Jian attacked but did not overcome him; because of the Yue affair he was dismissed, and Xiangxian replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian besieged him without success, was dismissed over the Xu Yue affair, and Xiangxian took his place.

sentences.zh: 乃集士、漢兵七萬以討，鑒懼，仰藥死，擇那氏後立之。

translations.literal: He then gathered seventy thousand native and Han troops to punish him; Jian feared, took poison and died; a descendant of the Na clan was chosen and installed.
translations.idiomatic: He then assembled seventy thousand native and Han troops for the punitive expedition; Na Jian, in terror, took poison and died, and a Na clansman was chosen to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部右侍郎，總督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of War and made overall commander of military affairs in the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Vice Minister of War and put in overall charge of military affairs in the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 賊魁徐銓等糾倭橫海上，檄副使汪柏等擊斬之。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftains Xu Qian and others gathered Wokou and rampaged on the sea; he dispatched Vice Commissioner Wang Bai and others to strike and behead them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit leaders Xu Qian and others rallied Wokou pirates who raided the coast; he dispatched Vice Commissioner Wang Bai and others, who killed them.

sentences.zh: 廣西賊黃父將等擾慶遠，搗其巢，大獲。

translations.literal: The Guangxi bandits Huang Fujiang and others harassed Qingyuan; he stormed their nest and won great gains.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi bandits led by Huang Fujiang harassed Qingyuan; he stormed their stronghold with great success.

sentences.zh: 予象賢一子官。

translations.literal: One of Xiangxian's sons was granted an official post.
translations.idiomatic: One of Xiangxian's sons was granted an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 入佐南京兵部。

translations.literal: He entered to assist at the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an assistant at the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 被劾，回籍聽勘。

translations.literal: He was impeached, returned to his native place, and awaited investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached, he returned home to await investigation.

sentences.zh: 家居十年，起太仆卿。

translations.literal: He lived at home ten years, then was raised as chief minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years at home he was recalled as chief minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 復以右副都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: Again he served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 召拜兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Left Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 年老引去。

translations.literal: Old in years, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing in age, he retired.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 翁萬達，字仁夫，揭陽人。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda, style name Renfu, was a man of Jieyang.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda, courtesy name Renfu, was a native of Jieyang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiajing year 5.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中，出為梧州知府。

translations.literal: After a second promotion he became a director; he went out as prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted twice to director, he then went out as prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 鹹寧侯仇鸞鎮兩廣，縱部卒為虐。

translations.literal: Marquis Qiu Luan of Xianning held command in the Two Guangs and allowed his subordinate troops to commit oppression.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Qiu Luan of Xianning held command in the Two Guangs and let his troops run rampant.

sentences.zh: 萬達縛其尤橫者，杖之。

translations.literal: Wanda bound the most arrogant of them and had them beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Wanda seized the worst offenders among them and had them flogged.

sentences.zh: 閱四年，聲績大著。

translations.literal: After four years his reputation and achievements were greatly notable.
translations.idiomatic: Within four years his reputation and record were greatly established.

sentences.zh: 會朝議將討安南，擢萬達廣西副使，專辦安南事。

translations.literal: It happened that the court deliberated on punishing Annam; Wanda was promoted to vice commissioner of Guangxi to handle Annam affairs exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: When the court began planning a punitive expedition against Annam, Wanda was promoted to vice commissioner of Guangxi to handle the campaign exclusively.

sentences.zh: 萬達請於總督張經曰：「莫登庸大言『中國不能正土官弒逆罪，安能問我』。

translations.literal: Wanda requested of Governor-General Zhang Jing, saying: "Mac Dang Dung loudly declares, 'China cannot punish native officials for regicide and treason—how can it question me?'
translations.idiomatic: Wanda appealed to Governor-General Zhang Jing: "Mac Dang Dung loudly declares, 'China cannot punish native officials for regicide—how can it question me?'

sentences.zh: 今憑祥州土舍李寰弒其土官珍，思恩府土目盧回煽九司亂，龍州土舍趙楷殺從子燧、煖，又結田州人韋應殺燧弟寶，斷藤峽瑤侯公丁負固。

translations.literal: Now native clerk Li Huan of Pingxiang Prefecture murdered his native official Zhen; native chieftain Lu Hui of Si'en Prefecture stirred the Nine Offices to rebellion; native clerk Zhao Kai of Longzhou killed his nephews Sui and Nuan, and also joined Tianzhou man Wei Ying in killing Sui's younger brother Bao; the Yao chieftain Hou Gongding of Duanteng Gorge held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Right now Li Huan, a native clerk of Pingxiang, has murdered his native official Zhen; Lu Hui, a native chieftain of Si'en, has incited the Nine Offices to revolt; Zhao Kai of Longzhou has killed his nephews Sui and Nuan and, with Wei Ying of Tianzhou, killed Sui's brother Bao; and the Yao leader Hou Gongding holds fast in Duanteng Gorge.

sentences.zh: 此曹同惡共濟，一旦約為內應，我且不自保。

translations.literal: These fellows share in evil and aid one another; once they agree on internal cooperation, we will not even be able to protect ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: These men are united in villainy; if they ever agreed to serve as inner collaborators, we could not even protect ourselves.

sentences.zh: 先擒此數人問罪，安南易下耳。

translations.literal: First seize these several men and interrogate them for crimes—Annam will then be easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: Seize these men first and bring them to justice, and Annam will fall easily."

sentences.zh: 」經曰：「然，惟君之所為。

translations.literal: Jing said: "So it is; do as you will."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing replied: "True—do as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 」於是誅寰、應，擒回，招還九司，誘殺楷，佯系訟公丁者紿公丁，執諸坐。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huan and Ying were executed, Hui was captured, the Nine Offices were summoned back, Kai was lured and killed; those pretending to be litigants in Gongding's case deceived Gongding and seized him in court.
translations.idiomatic: He then executed Li Huan and Wei Ying, captured Lu Hui, restored the Nine Offices, lured and killed Zhao Kai, and, using men feigning legal disputes to trap Hou Gongding, seized him in court.

sentences.zh: 以兩軍破平其巢。

translations.literal: With two armies he broke and pacified their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Two armies then stormed and leveled their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 又議割四峒屬南寧，降峒豪黃賢相。

translations.literal: He also proposed ceding the Four Caves to Nanning and accepting the surrender of cave magnate Huang Xianxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed assigning the Four Caves to Nanning and accepting the surrender of cave chieftain Huang Xianxiang.

sentences.zh: 登庸始懼。

translations.literal: Dang Dung then first grew fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Mac Dang Dung grow alarmed.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江右參政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Administrative Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Administrative Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 經以征安南非萬達不可，奏留之，乃命以參政蒞廣西。

translations.literal: Jing held that the Annam expedition could not proceed without Wanda; he memorialized to retain him, and Wanda was then ordered to go to Guangxi as administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing insisted the Annam expedition required Wanda and memorialized to keep him; Wanda was then ordered to Guangxi as administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 已而毛伯溫集兵進剿，萬達上書伯溫，言：「揖讓而告成功，上策也。

translations.literal: Before long Mao Bowen gathered troops for a punitive advance; Wanda wrote Bowen, saying: "To achieve success through yielding ceremony is the highest strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Mao Bowen mustered troops for a punitive advance; Wanda wrote Bowen: "Winning through courtesy and submission is the best course.

sentences.zh: 懾之以不敢不從，中策也。

translations.literal: To intimidate so that one dares not refuse is the middle strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Intimidating them into compliance is the middle course.

sentences.zh: 芟夷絕滅，終為下策。

translations.literal: To mow down and utterly exterminate is ultimately the lowest strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Extermination is the worst option."

sentences.zh: 」伯溫然之。

translations.literal: Bowen approved.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen agreed.

sentences.zh: 會獲安南諜者丁南傑，萬達解其縛，厚遇，遣之去，怵以天朝兵威。

translations.literal: It happened that the Annam spy Ding Nanjie was captured; Wanda released his bonds, treated him generously, sent him away, and intimidated him with the military might of the Heavenly Court.
translations.idiomatic: An Annamese spy named Ding Nanjie was captured; Wanda freed him, treated him generously, sent him home, and impressed upon him the might of the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 登庸大懼，乃詣伯溫乞降。

translations.literal: Dang Dung was greatly afraid and then went to Bowen to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Mac Dang Dung, deeply alarmed, went to Bowen to sue for surrender.

sentences.zh: 是役也，萬達功最，賞不逾常格。

translations.literal: In this campaign Wanda's merit was greatest, yet reward did not exceed the usual measure.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Wanda's merit ranked first, yet his reward did not exceed the usual scale.

sentences.zh: 然帝知其能，遷四川按察使。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor knew his ability and transferred him to provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor recognized his ability and made him provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 歷陜西左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Left and Right Administrative Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Left and Right Administrative Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，擢右副都御史，巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋進兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，代翟鵬總督宣、大、山西、保定軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Right Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, replacing Zhai Peng as overall commander of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, Shanxi, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, succeeding Zhai Peng as overall commander of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, Shanxi, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 劾罷宣府總兵官郤永、副總兵姜奭，薦何卿、趙卿、沈希儀。

translations.literal: He impeached and dismissed the Xuanfu regional commander Qi Yong and vice regional commander Jiang Yi, and recommended He Qing, Zhao Qing, and Shen Xiyi.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and removed Xuanfu regional commander Qi Yong and vice commander Jiang Yi, and recommended He Qing, Zhao Qing, and Shen Xiyi.

sentences.zh: 趙卿遂代永。

translations.literal: Zhao Qing then replaced Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qing then replaced Xi Yong as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 萬達謹偵候，明賞罰。

translations.literal: Wanda was careful in reconnaissance, clear in rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda kept strict watch on enemy movements and made rewards and punishments unmistakably clear.

sentences.zh: 每當防秋，發卒乘障，陰遣卒傾朱於油，察離次者朱其處。

translations.literal: Each time in autumn defense, troops were sent to man the ramparts; secretly he had soldiers pour vermilion into oil and mark the places of those who left their posts.
translations.idiomatic: During each autumn defense season, when troops manned the ramparts, he secretly had men mix vermilion into oil and mark any spot where a soldier had left his post.

sentences.zh: 卒歸輒縛，毋敢復離次者。

translations.literal: When soldiers returned they were bound at once; none dared leave their posts again.
translations.idiomatic: When the men came back, offenders were bound on the spot, and no one dared leave his post again.

sentences.zh: 嚴殺降禁，違輒抵死。

translations.literal: He strictly forbade killing surrenderers; violators were punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: He strictly forbade the killing of surrenderers, and anyone who violated the rule was put to death.

sentences.zh: 得降人，撫之如所親，以是益知敵情。

translations.literal: When he obtained surrenderers, he treated them like his own kin, and thereby learned more about the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When he took surrenderers, he treated them as if they were his own kin, and so learned ever more about the enemy.

sentences.zh: 寇數萬騎犯大同中路，入鐵裹門，故總兵官張達力戰卻之。

translations.literal: Bandits in tens of thousands of horsemen invaded the middle route at Datong, entered Tiego Gate; the former regional commander Zhang Da fought hard and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders in tens of thousands of horsemen struck the middle route at Datong and entered Tiego Gate; the former regional commander Zhang Da fought fiercely and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 又犯鵓鴿谷，參將張鳳、諸生王邦直等戰死。

translations.literal: They invaded again at Bogue Valley; Assistant Commander Zhang Feng, scholar Wang Bangzhi, and others died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They struck again at Bogue Valley, where Assistant Commander Zhang Feng, the scholar Wang Bangzhi, and others were killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 萬達與總兵官周尚文備陽和，而遣騎四出邀擊，頗有斬獲。

translations.literal: Wanda and the regional commander Zhou Shangwen prepared at Yanghe, while sending cavalry out in all directions to intercept; there were considerable kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda and regional commander Zhou Shangwen held Yanghe while dispatching cavalry in all directions to intercept the enemy, with considerable kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 寇登山，見官兵大集，乃引去。

translations.literal: The bandits climbed a mountain, saw government troops gathered in force, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders climbed a hill, saw government troops massed below, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜敕獎賚。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict was issued with rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached the throne, the emperor issued an edict commending and rewarding them.

sentences.zh: 屢疏請修築邊墻，議自大同東路陽和口至宣府西陽河，須帑銀二十九萬。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized requesting construction of border walls, proposing from Yanghekou on the eastern Datong route to Xiyang River in Xuanfu, requiring 290,000 taels from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized asking to build border walls from Yanghekou on the eastern Datong route to Xiyang River in Xuanfu, at an estimated cost of 290,000 taels from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 帝已許之，兵部撓其議，以大同舊有二邊，不當復於邊內築墻。

translations.literal: The emperor had already approved, but the Ministry of War obstructed the plan, saying Datong already had inner and outer lines and walls should not be built again inside the border.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already approved, but the Ministry of War blocked the plan, arguing that Datong already had inner and outer defense lines and that walls should not be built again inside the border.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 乃自大同東路天城、陽和、開山口諸處為墻百二十八里，堡七，墩臺百五十四；

translations.literal: So from Tiancheng, Yanghe, Kaishankou and other places on the eastern Datong route he built walls of 128 li, 7 forts, and 154 beacon platforms;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore built 128 li of wall, seven forts, and 154 beacon platforms from Tiancheng, Yanghe, Kaishankou, and other points on the eastern Datong route;

sentences.zh: 宣府西路西陽河、洗馬林、張家口諸處為墻六十四里，敵臺十。

translations.literal: On the western Xuanfu route at Xiyang River, Ximalin, Zhangjiakou and elsewhere, walls of 64 li and 10 enemy towers.
translations.idiomatic: and on the western Xuanfu route at Xiyang River, Ximalin, Zhangjiakou, and elsewhere, 64 li of wall and ten enemy towers.

sentences.zh: 斬崖削坡五十里。

translations.literal: Cliffs were cut and slopes shaved for 50 li.
translations.idiomatic: Cliffs were cut back and slopes leveled over fifty li.

sentences.zh: 工五十余日成。

translations.literal: The work was completed in a little over fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: The work was finished in a little over fifty days.

sentences.zh: 進右都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 發代府宗室充灼等叛謀，進左都御史。

translations.literal: He exposed the treasonous plot of Dai Prefecture imperial clansmen including Chongzhuo and was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After exposing the treasonous plot of the Dai Prefecture imperial clansman Chongzhuo and others, he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 已，會宣、大、山西鎮巡官議上邊防修守事宜，其略曰：

translations.literal: Subsequently, the inspecting and pacifying officials of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi convened to submit proposals on border defense maintenance; the gist was:
translations.idiomatic: Later, the inspecting and pacifying officials of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi met to submit proposals on border defense; the gist was as follows:

sentences.zh: 山西起保德州黃河岸，歷偏頭，抵老營二百五十四里。

translations.literal: Shanxi runs from the Yellow River bank at Baode Prefecture, through Piantou, to Laoying, 254 li.
translations.idiomatic: In Shanxi, the outer line runs 254 li from the Yellow River bank at Baode Prefecture through Piantou to Laoying.

sentences.zh: 大同西路起丫角山，歷中北二路，東抵東陽河鎮口臺六百四十七里。

translations.literal: The western Datong route runs from Yajiao Mountain, through the middle and north routes, east to the Zhenkoutai at Dongyang River, 647 li.
translations.idiomatic: The western Datong route runs 647 li from Yajiao Mountain through the middle and northern routes east to Zhenkoutai at Dongyang River.

sentences.zh: 宣府起西陽河，歷中北二路，東抵永寧四海冶千二十三里。

translations.literal: Xuanfu runs from Xiyang River, through the middle and north routes, east to Yongning and Sihaiye, 1,023 li.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanfu runs 1,023 li from Xiyang River through the middle and northern routes east to Yongning and Sihaiye.

sentences.zh: 凡千九百二十四里，皆逼巨寇，險在外，所謂極邊也。

translations.literal: In all 1,924 li, all pressing on great bandits, with danger on the outside—the so-called outermost border.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether 1,924 li—all facing major raiders, with the danger lying outward—constitute what is called the outermost border.

sentences.zh: 山西老營堡轉南而東，歷寧武、雁門，至平刑關八百里。

translations.literal: From Laoying Fort in Shanxi, turning south then east, through Ningwu and Yanmen to Pingxing Pass, 800 li.
translations.idiomatic: From Laoying Fort in Shanxi, turning south and then east through Ningwu and Yanmen to Pingxing Pass is 800 li.

sentences.zh: 又轉南而東，歷龍泉、倒馬、紫荊之吳王口、插箭嶺、浮圖峪，至沿河口千七十餘里。

translations.literal: Again turning south then east, through Longquan, Daoma, and Zijing's Wuwangkou, Chajian Ridge, and Futu Valley to Yanhekou, more than 1,070 li.
translations.idiomatic: Turning south and east again through Longquan, Daoma, and Zijing—Wuwangkou, Chajian Ridge, and Futu Valley—to Yanhekou is more than 1,070 li.

sentences.zh: 又東北，歷高崖、白羊，至居庸關一百八十餘里。

translations.literal: Again northeast, through Gaoya and Baiyang to Juyong Pass, more than 180 li.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast from there through Gaoya and Baiyang to Juyong Pass is more than 180 li.

sentences.zh: 凡二千五十餘里，皆峻山層岡，險在內，所謂次邊也。

translations.literal: In all more than 2,050 li, all steep mountains and layered ridges, with danger on the inside—the so-called secondary border.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether more than 2,050 li of steep mountains and layered ridges, with the danger lying inward, constitute what is called the secondary border.

sentences.zh: 外邊，大同最難守，次宣府，次山西之偏、老。

translations.literal: Of the outer border, Datong is hardest to defend, next Xuanfu, next Piantou and Laoying in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Of the outer border, Datong is the hardest to hold, then Xuanfu, then Piantou and Laoying in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 大同最難守者，北路。

translations.literal: The hardest to defend in Datong is the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: Within Datong, the northern route is the hardest to defend.

sentences.zh: 宣府最難守者，西路。

translations.literal: The hardest to defend in Xuanfu is the western route.
translations.idiomatic: Within Xuanfu, the western route is the hardest to defend.

sentences.zh: 山西偏關以西百五十里，恃河為險；

translations.literal: West of Pianguan in Shanxi for 150 li, relying on the river as defense;
translations.idiomatic: West of Pianguan in Shanxi, for 150 li the defense relies on the river;

sentences.zh: 偏關以東百有四里，略與大同西路等。

translations.literal: East of Pianguan for 104 li, roughly equal to the western Datong route.
translations.idiomatic: east of Pianguan, for 104 li, conditions are much like those on the western Datong route.

sentences.zh: 內邊，紫荊、寧武、雁門為要，次則居庸、倒馬、龍泉、平刑。

translations.literal: Of the inner border, Zijing, Ningwu, and Yanmen are critical; next come Juyong, Daoma, Longquan, and Pingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Of the inner border, Zijing, Ningwu, and Yanmen are the key points; next come Juyong, Daoma, Longquan, and Pingxing.

sentences.zh: 邇年寇犯山西，必自大同；

translations.literal: In recent years when bandits invaded Shanxi, they always came from Datong;
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, raids into Shanxi have always entered from Datong;

sentences.zh: 犯紫荊，必自宣府。

translations.literal: When they invaded Zijing, they always came from Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: and raids on Zijing have always entered from Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 先年山西防秋，止守外邊偏、老一帶，歲發班軍六千人備禦，大同仍置兵，寧、雁為聲援。

translations.literal: In earlier years Shanxi autumn defense held only the outer border strip of Piantou and Laoying, sending 6,000 rotating troops each year for defense; Datong still kept troops, with Ningwu and Yanmen as support.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years Shanxi's autumn defense held only the outer Piantou–Laoying strip, sending 6,000 rotating troops each year while Datong kept its own forces and Ningwu and Yanmen served as reserves.

sentences.zh: 比棄極沖，守次邊，非守要之意。

translations.literal: Now abandoning the most critical points and defending the secondary border is not the intent of holding key positions.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the most critical points and defend only the secondary border is not what holding the key passes should mean.

sentences.zh: 宣府亦專備西、中二路，而北路空虛。

translations.literal: Xuanfu also concentrated on the western and middle routes, leaving the northern route empty.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanfu likewise concentrated on the western and middle routes, leaving the northern route undefended.

sentences.zh: 且連年三鎮防秋，征調遼、陜兵馬，糜糧賞不訾，恐難持久。

translations.literal: Moreover, for years the three garrisons' autumn defense has requisitioned troops from Liaodong and Shaanxi, consuming grain and rewards beyond reckoning, and may not be sustainable.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for years the three garrisons' autumn defense has drawn troops from Liaodong and Shaanxi, consuming grain and rewards beyond reckoning—a burden that cannot be sustained indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 並守之議，實為善經。

translations.literal: The proposal to defend both lines together is truly sound policy.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal to defend both lines together is truly sound long-term policy.

sentences.zh: 外邊四時皆防，城堡兵各有分地，冬春徂夏，不必參錯征發。

translations.literal: The outer border should be defended in all four seasons; garrison troops at forts and castles each have assigned sectors, from winter and spring through summer, without need for mixed requisitioning.
translations.idiomatic: The outer border should be defended year-round, with garrison troops at each fort assigned fixed sectors from winter through summer, without the need for haphazard requisitioning.

sentences.zh: 若泥往事臨時調遣，近者數十里，遠者百餘里，首尾不相應。

translations.literal: If one clings to past practice of last-minute dispatch, the near are several tens of li away and the far more than a hundred li, with head and tail unable to respond to each other.
translations.idiomatic: If one clings to the old practice of last-minute dispatch, nearby units may be several tens of li away and distant ones more than a hundred li, with no way for front and rear to coordinate.

sentences.zh: 萬一如往年潰墻而入，越關而南，京師震駭，方始征調，何益事機？

translations.literal: If by any chance, as in past years, they breach the wall and enter, cross the passes southward, and the capital is shaken in alarm—only then to begin requisitioning—what good is that to the moment?
translations.idiomatic: If, as in past years, raiders breach the wall, cross the passes southward, and the capital is thrown into alarm before troops are even mobilized, what good will that do?

sentences.zh: 擺邊之兵，未可遽罷。

translations.literal: The troops deployed along the border must not be hastily disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: The troops deployed along the border must not be disbanded hastily.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰「王公設險以守其國」。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says, "Kings and dukes set up defenses to guard their states."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Kings and dukes set up defenses to guard their states."

sentences.zh: 「設」之雲者，築垣乘障、資人力之謂也。

translations.literal: What is meant by "set up" is building walls and ramparts and relying on human strength.
translations.idiomatic: What "set up" means is building walls and ramparts and relying on human labor.

sentences.zh: 山川之險，險與彼共。

translations.literal: The danger of mountains and rivers is danger shared with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The advantage of mountains and rivers is an advantage shared with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 垣塹之險，險為我專。

translations.literal: The danger of walls and moats is danger ours alone.
translations.idiomatic: The advantage of walls and moats is an advantage ours alone.

sentences.zh: 百人之堡，非千人不能攻，以有垣塹可憑也。

translations.literal: A fort of a hundred men cannot be taken by less than a thousand, because there are walls and moats to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: A fort of a hundred men cannot be taken by fewer than a thousand, because walls and moats give defenders something to stand on.

sentences.zh: 修邊之役，必當再舉。

translations.literal: The work of repairing the border must be undertaken again.
translations.idiomatic: Border repair must be undertaken again.

sentences.zh: 夫定規畫，度工費，二者修邊之事；

translations.literal: Setting plans and estimating labor costs—these two are matters of border repair;
translations.idiomatic: Setting plans and estimating costs are matters of border repair;

sentences.zh: 慎防秋，並兵力，重責成，量征調，實邊堡，明出塞，計供億，節財用，八者守邊之事。

translations.literal: Careful autumn defense, combining military strength, heavy accountability, measured requisitioning, strengthening border forts, clear rules for going beyond the border, calculating supplies, and economizing expenditures—these eight are matters of border defense.
translations.idiomatic: careful autumn defense, combining forces, strict accountability, measured requisitioning, strengthening border forts, clear rules for campaigns beyond the border, calculating supplies, and economizing expenditures—these eight are matters of border defense.

sentences.zh: 因條十事上之，帝悉報許。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted ten items in detail; the emperor approved them all.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted ten detailed proposals, and the emperor approved them all.

sentences.zh: 乃請帑銀六十萬兩，修大同西路、宣府東路邊墻，凡八百里。

translations.literal: He then requested 600,000 taels from the treasury to repair border walls on the western Datong route and eastern Xuanfu route, 800 li in all.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested 600,000 taels from the treasury to build border walls on the western Datong route and eastern Xuanfu route—800 li in all.

sentences.zh: 工成，予一子官。

translations.literal: When the work was completed, one of his sons was granted an official post.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was completed, one of his sons was granted an official post.

sentences.zh: 萬達精心計，善鉤校，墻堞近遠，濠塹深廣，曲盡其宜。

translations.literal: Wanda planned meticulously and was skilled at inspection; wall towers near and far, moats deep and wide—all were made to fit perfectly.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda planned meticulously and inspected every detail; the spacing of towers, and the depth and width of moats, were all adjusted to perfection.

sentences.zh: 寇乃不敢輕犯。

translations.literal: The bandits then did not dare invade lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders then did not dare attack lightly.

sentences.zh: 墻內戍者得以暇耕牧，邊費亦日省。

translations.literal: Garrison troops inside the wall could farm and herd in their spare time, and border expenses were also reduced day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison troops inside the walls could farm and herd in their spare time, and border expenses dwindled day by day.

sentences.zh: 初，客兵防秋，歲帑金一百五十余萬，添發且數十萬，其後減省幾半。

translations.literal: At first, guest troops for autumn defense cost the treasury more than 1.5 million taels a year, with additional disbursements of several hundred thousand; afterward expenditures were cut by nearly half.
translations.idiomatic: At first, guest troops for autumn defense cost the treasury more than 1.5 million taels a year, with supplemental payments of several hundred thousand more; afterward expenditures were cut by nearly half.

sentences.zh: 又議掣山西兵並力守大同，巡撫孫繼魯沮之。

translations.literal: He also proposed pulling Shanxi troops to join forces in defending Datong; Grand Coordinator Sun Jilu obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed pulling Shanxi troops to concentrate on defending Datong, but Grand Coordinator Sun Jilu blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 帝為逮繼魯，悉納萬達言。

translations.literal: The emperor had Jilu arrested and fully adopted Wanda's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Sun Jilu arrested and fully adopted Weng Wanda's proposals.

sentences.zh: 萬達更事久，帝深倚之，所請無不從，獨言俺答貢事與帝意左。

translations.literal: Wanda had long experience in affairs; the emperor relied on him deeply and granted every request—only his words on Altan's tribute matter went against the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda had long experience in frontier affairs; the emperor relied on him deeply and granted every request—only his advice on Altan Khan's tribute proposals ran counter to the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 先是，二十一年，俺答阿不孩使石天爵等款鎮遠堡求貢。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the twenty-first year, Altan Abunai sent Shi Tianjue and others to present themselves at Zhenyuan Fort seeking tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the twenty-first year of the reign, Altan Abunai sent Shi Tianjue and others to Zhenyuan Fort to sue for tribute.

sentences.zh: 言小王子等九部牧青山，艷中國縑帛，入掠止人畜，所得寡，且不能無亡失，故令天爵輸誠。

translations.literal: They said the Little Prince and nine tribes pastured at Qingshan, coveted Chinese silks, and in raids took only people and livestock with meager gains and unavoidable losses, so Tianjue was sent to offer sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: They said the Little Prince and nine tribes pastured at Qingshan, coveted Chinese silks, and gained little from raids beyond people and livestock while suffering unavoidable losses—hence Tianjue was sent to offer their sincerity.

sentences.zh: 朝議不納。

translations.literal: Court deliberation did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The court rejected the proposal.

sentences.zh: 天爵等復至，巡撫龍大有執之。

translations.literal: Tianjue and others came again; Grand Coordinator Long Dayou seized them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianjue and his party came again, Grand Coordinator Long Dayou seized them.

sentences.zh: 大有進一官，將吏悉遷擢，磔天爵於市。

translations.literal: Dayou was promoted one rank, officers and officials were all promoted, and Tianjue was dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Long Dayou was promoted one rank, his officers were all promoted, and Tianjue was dismembered in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 寇怒，大入，屠村堡，信使絕五年。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged, invaded on a large scale, slaughtered villages and forts, and envoys were cut off for five years.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongols were enraged, raided on a large scale, slaughtered villages and forts, and diplomatic contact was severed for five years.

sentences.zh: 會玉林衛百戶楊威為所掠，威詭能定貢市，遂釋還。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Wei, a company commander of Yulin Guard, was captured; Wei falsely claimed he could settle tribute and trade, and was then released.
translations.idiomatic: Company commander Yang Wei of Yulin Guard was captured; he falsely claimed he could arrange tribute and trade, and was then released.

sentences.zh: 俺答阿不孩復遣使款大同左衛塞，邊帥家丁董寶等狃天爵前事，復殺之，以首功報。

translations.literal: Altan Abunai again sent envoys to present themselves at the Datong Left Guard pass; the border commander's household retainers Dong Bao and others, emboldened by Tianjue's earlier case, killed them again and reported it as a head-count victory.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Abunai again sent envoys to sue for peace at the Datong Left Guard pass; the border commander's household retainers Dong Bao and others, emboldened by the Tianjue affair, killed them again and reported it as a victory of severed heads.

sentences.zh: 萬達言：「北敵，弘治前歲入貢，疆場稍寧。

translations.literal: Wanda said: "The northern enemy, before Hongzhi, entered tribute yearly and the frontier was somewhat calm.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda said, "Before Hongzhi, the northern enemy paid tribute yearly and the frontier was relatively calm.

sentences.zh: 自虞臺嶺之戰覆我師，漸輕中國，侵犯四十余年。

translations.literal: Since the battle at Yutailing destroyed our army, they gradually looked down on China and have invaded for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Since the battle at Yutailing destroyed our army, they have gradually looked down on China and raided for more than forty years.

sentences.zh: 石天爵之事，臣嘗痛邊臣失計。

translations.literal: In the matter of Shi Tianjue, your subject once grieved that border officials had miscalculated.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shi Tianjue affair, I grieved that the border officials had miscalculated.

sentences.zh: 今復通款，即不許，當善相諭遣。

translations.literal: Now they again open relations; even if tribute is not granted, they should be kindly instructed and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have opened relations again; even if tribute is not granted, they should be courteously instructed and sent away.

sentences.zh: 誘而殺之，此何理也？

translations.literal: To lure and kill them—what principle is this?
translations.idiomatic: To lure them in and kill them—what principle is that?

sentences.zh: 請亟誅寶等，榜塞上，明告以朝廷德意，解其蓄怨構兵之謀。

translations.literal: I ask that Bao and others be promptly executed, a proclamation posted on the border, and the court's benevolent intent clearly announced, to dissolve their accumulated grievances and plans for war.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Dong Bao and his accomplices be executed at once, a proclamation posted on the border, and the court's benevolent intent clearly announced, to dissolve their accumulated grievances and war plans.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，俺答阿不孩復奉印信番文，欲詣邊陳款。

translations.literal: Before long, Altan Abunai again presented his seal and a Mongol document, wishing to come to the border to declare sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Altan Abunai again presented his seal and a Mongol document, wishing to come to the border to declare his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 萬達為奏曰：「今屆秋，彼可一逞。

translations.literal: Wanda memorialized: "Now it is autumn; they may strike once.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda memorialized, "Autumn is here, and they may yet strike once.

sentences.zh: 乃屢被殺戮，猶請貢不已者，緣入犯則利在部落，獲貢則利歸其長。

translations.literal: Yet though repeatedly killed, they still ceaselessly request tribute, because in invasion the profit goes to the tribes, while in receiving tribute the profit goes to their chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though their envoys have been killed again and again, they still ceaselessly request tribute, because raids profit the tribes while tribute profits their chief.

sentences.zh: 處之克當，邊患可弭。

translations.literal: If handled properly, border troubles can be quelled.
translations.idiomatic: If handled properly, border troubles can be quelled.

sentences.zh: 若臣等封疆臣，貢亦備，不貢亦備，不緣此懈也。

translations.literal: As frontier officials like us, we prepare whether tribute comes or not, and will not slacken on this account.
translations.idiomatic: As frontier officials, we will remain prepared whether tribute is granted or not, and will not slacken our defenses on that account.

sentences.zh: 」兵部尚書陳經等言敵難信，請敕邊臣詰實，責萬達十日內回奏。

translations.literal: " Minister of War Chen Jing and others said the enemy was hard to trust, asked that border officials be ordered to verify, and charged Wanda to reply within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of War Chen Jing and others said the enemy could not be trusted, asked that border officials verify the matter, and ordered Weng Wanda to reply within ten days.

sentences.zh: 萬達還其使，與約。

translations.literal: Wanda returned their envoy and made an agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda sent their envoy back and made an agreement.

sentences.zh: 至期，使者不至。

translations.literal: When the deadline came, the envoy did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: When the deadline came, the envoy did not arrive.

sentences.zh: 萬達慮帝督過，以使者去無可究為辭。

translations.literal: Wanda feared the emperor would press him for fault and used the excuse that the envoy had left and nothing could be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda feared the emperor would hold him accountable and pleaded that the envoy had already left and nothing could be investigated.

sentences.zh: 已而使狎至，牢拒之，好言慰答而已。

translations.literal: Soon envoys came repeatedly; he firmly refused them, offering only kind words in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Soon envoys came repeatedly; he firmly refused them, offering only polite words in reply.

sentences.zh: 俺答以通好，散處其眾，不設備，亦不殺哨卒。

translations.literal: Altan, because of the overtures, dispersed his followers, made no preparations, and did not kill sentry soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the overtures, Altan dispersed his followers, made no preparations, and did not kill sentry soldiers.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復至，詞益恭。

translations.literal: Before long they came again, their words ever more deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they came again, their language ever more deferential.

sentences.zh: 萬達又為奏曰：「敵懇懇求貢，去而復來。

translations.literal: Wanda memorialized again: "The enemy earnestly seeks tribute, leaving and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda memorialized again, "The enemy earnestly seeks tribute, leaving and returning.

sentences.zh: 今宣、大興版築，正當羈縻，使無擾。

translations.literal: Now Xuanfu and Datong are undertaking large-scale construction; this is exactly the time to restrain and attach them, so they do not disturb us.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanfu and Datong are now undertaking large-scale construction; this is exactly the time to keep them in check so they do not disturb us.

sentences.zh: 請限以地、以人、以時。

translations.literal: I ask that limits be set by place, by persons, and by time.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that limits be set on place, personnel, and time.

sentences.zh: 悉聽，即許之貢；

translations.literal: If all are accepted, then grant tribute;
translations.idiomatic: If they accept all the limits, then grant tribute;

sentences.zh: 不聽，則曲在彼，即拒絕之。

translations.literal: If they do not accept, the fault lies with them, and we may refuse.
translations.idiomatic: if they refuse, the fault lies with them, and we may reject them.

sentences.zh: 」帝責其瀆奏，卒不許。

translations.literal: " The emperor rebuked him for importunate memorializing and ultimately did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor rebuked him for importunate memorializing and ultimately refused.

sentences.zh: 蓋是時曾銑有復套之議，夏言主之，故力絀貢議，且以復套事行諸邊臣議之。

translations.literal: At that time Zeng Xian had a proposal to recover the Ordos, which Xia Yan supported, so tribute was forcefully blocked, and the matter of recovering the Ordos was sent to border officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zeng Xian had proposed recovering the Ordos, which Xia Yan supported, so tribute was forcefully blocked, and the Ordos recovery plan was sent to border officials for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 萬達議曰：

translations.literal: Wanda deliberated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda submitted his opinion:

sentences.zh: 河套本中國故壤。

translations.literal: The Ordos was originally China's old territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Ordos was originally Chinese territory.

sentences.zh: 成祖三犁王庭，殘其部落，舍黃河，衛東勝。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor thrice plowed the royal court, destroyed their tribes, relied on the Yellow River, and guarded Dongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle thrice led campaigns deep into the steppe, shattered the Mongol tribes, took the Yellow River as his line of defense, and garrisoned Dongsheng.

sentences.zh: 後又撤東勝以就延綏，套地遂淪失。

translations.literal: Later Dongsheng was again withdrawn in favor of Yan-sui, and the Ordos territory was thus lost.
translations.idiomatic: Later Dongsheng was abandoned in turn for Yan-sui, and the Ordos was lost entirely.

sentences.zh: 然正統、弘治間，我未守，彼亦未取。

translations.literal: Yet in the Zhengtong and Hongzhi periods, we did not hold it, and they also did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet during the Zhengtong and Hongzhi reigns, China did not hold it, and the Mongols did not take it either.

sentences.zh: 乃因循畫地守，捐天險，失沃野之利。

translations.literal: Then by routine we marked boundaries to defend, surrendered Heaven's strategic barriers, and lost the benefit of fertile plains.
translations.idiomatic: We fell into the habit of defending drawn boundaries, gave up natural strongholds, and forfeited the wealth of the open grasslands.

sentences.zh: 弘治前，我猶歲搜套，後乃任彼出入，盤據其中，畜牧生養。

translations.literal: Before Hongzhi we still searched the Ordos annually; afterward we allowed them to come and go at will, and they entrenched themselves within it, raising livestock and multiplying.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Hongzhi era we still raided into the Ordos each year; afterward we let them come and go freely until they entrenched themselves there, grazing and multiplying their herds.

sentences.zh: 譬之為家，成業久矣，欲一舉復之，毋乃不易乎！

translations.literal: Compared to a household whose established holdings have long endured, to wish to recover them all at one stroke—would that not be difficult!
translations.idiomatic: It is like a family estate held for generations: to try to reclaim it all in a single stroke would be far from easy!

sentences.zh: 提軍深入，山川之險易，途徑之迂直，水草之有無，皆未熟知。

translations.literal: If we lead troops deep in, whether mountains and rivers are dangerous or easy, whether routes are winding or straight, whether water and fodder exist or not—we are none of these thoroughly familiar with.
translations.idiomatic: If we march deep into enemy country, we lack detailed knowledge of terrain—where mountains offer advantage, which routes twist or run straight, where water and pasture can be found.

sentences.zh: 我馬出塞三日已疲，彼騎一呼可集。

translations.literal: Our horses, three days out of the frontier pass, are already exhausted; their horsemen at one call can assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Our horses are worn out after three days beyond the frontier, while their riders rally at a single summons.

sentences.zh: 我軍數萬眾，緩行持重則備益固，疾行趨利則輜重在後。

translations.literal: Our army of tens of thousands—if we advance slowly and steadily our defenses grow stronger; if we hurry for gain our baggage train is left behind.
translations.idiomatic: An army of tens of thousands faces a cruel choice: advance slowly and our defenses hold, but rush for advantage and our supply train is left behind.

sentences.zh: 即得小利，歸師尚艱。

translations.literal: Even if we gain a small victory, the withdrawal will still be arduous.
translations.idiomatic: Even a small victory would leave a brutal withdrawal ahead.

sentences.zh: 倘失向導，全軍殆矣。

translations.literal: If we lose our guides, the whole army would be imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: Lose our guides, and the entire army is doomed.

sentences.zh: 彼遷徙遠近靡常。

translations.literal: Their migrations near and far have no fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: They migrate unpredictably, never staying in one place.

sentences.zh: 一戰之後，彼或保聚，或佯遁，笳角時動，壁壘相持，已離復合，終不渡河。

translations.literal: After one battle they may hold together or feign retreat; horns and conches sound from time to time, entrenchments face each other; having scattered they reunite, and in the end never cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: After a single clash they may rally or feign retreat; horns and drums sound intermittently as their camps stand firm—they scatter and reassemble, but never cross the river to give us the opening we need.

sentences.zh: 我軍於此，戰耶，退耶，兩相守耶？

translations.literal: For our army at this point—fight? retreat? or stand facing each other?
translations.idiomatic: What then for our army—fight, retreat, or stand locked in stalemate?

sentences.zh: 數萬眾出塞，亦必數萬眾援之，又以驍將通糧道，是皆至難而不可任者也。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands going beyond the frontier must also be supported by tens of thousands, and still need fierce generals to keep the supply route open—all these are tasks of utmost difficulty and not to be undertaken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands marching beyond the frontier require tens of thousands more in support, plus elite generals to keep supply lines open—all of this is extraordinarily difficult and should not be lightly attempted.

sentences.zh: 夫馳擊者彼所長，守險者我所便。

translations.literal: As for mounted striking, that is their strength; holding strategic barriers is our advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Charged raids are their strength; holding defensible terrain is ours.

sentences.zh: 弓矢利馳擊，火器利守險。

translations.literal: Bows and arrows favor mounted striking; firearms favor holding strategic barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Bows and arrows suit the charge; firearms suit static defense.

sentences.zh: 舍火器守險，與之馳擊於黃沙白草間，大非計。

translations.literal: Abandoning firearms and strategic defense to engage them in mounted combat amid yellow sand and white grass—this is very poor planning indeed.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon firearms and fortified positions and meet them in open steppe combat amid the dunes and grass would be disastrous strategy.

sentences.zh: 議者欲整六萬眾，為三歲期。

translations.literal: Those debating the matter wish to assemble sixty thousand troops for a three-year campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The advocates propose assembling sixty thousand men for a three-year campaign.

sentences.zh: 春夏馬瘦，彼弱，我利於征；

translations.literal: In spring and summer horses are lean, the enemy is weak, and we benefit from campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and summer horses are lean and the enemy weakened—we should attack then.

sentences.zh: 秋冬馬肥，彼強，我利於守。

translations.literal: In autumn and winter horses are fat, the enemy is strong, and we benefit from defending.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn and winter their horses are fat and they grow stronger—we should hold our defenses then.

sentences.zh: 春搜套，秋守邊，三舉彼必遠遁，我乃拒河守。

translations.literal: Spring raids into the Ordos, autumn frontier defense—three campaigns and they will surely flee far; then we hold at the river's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Raid the Ordos in spring, defend the frontier in autumn—after three such cycles the enemy must flee, and we can hold the river line.

sentences.zh: 夫馬肥瘦，我與敵共之。

translations.literal: As for whether horses are fat or lean, we and the enemy share the same conditions.
translations.idiomatic: Fat and lean seasons affect both sides equally.

sentences.zh: 即彼弱，然坐以待，懼其擾擊我，及彼強，又懼其報復我。

translations.literal: Even when they are weak, if we sit and wait, we fear they will harass and strike us; when they grow strong, we again fear their reprisal.
translations.idiomatic: When they are weak we cannot sit idle for fear of harassment; when they grow strong we dread their revenge.

sentences.zh: 且六萬之眾，千里襲人，一舉失利，議論蜂起，烏能待三？

translations.literal: Moreover, with sixty thousand troops raiding a thousand li, if one attempt fails, debate will swarm like bees—how can we wait for three?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, sixty thousand men raiding a thousand li away—one failure will bring a storm of criticism. How could we sustain three campaigns?

sentences.zh: 即三舉三勝，彼敗而守，終不渡河，版築亦無日。

translations.literal: Even if three campaigns bring three victories, they will defeat us by holding firm, never crossing the river—and there will never be a day for building fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Even three victories in three campaigns would leave them entrenched, never crossing the river—and we would never have the chance to build our fortifications.

sentences.zh: 議者見近時搗巢，恒獲首功，昔年城大同五堡，寇不深競，以為套易復。

translations.literal: The debaters see that in recent nest-raiding operations they constantly win head-count merit, and that years ago when five forts were built at Datong the raiders did not contest deeply—they therefore think the Ordos is easy to recover.
translations.idiomatic: Advocates point to recent raids that routinely yield trophies, and to the five Datong forts once built without fierce resistance—they conclude the Ordos can be easily retaken.

sentences.zh: 然搗巢，因其近塞，乘不備，勝則倏歸，舉足南向即家門。

translations.literal: Yet nest-raiding works because it is close to the frontier, taking them unawares; when victorious one returns swiftly—a step southward and one is at one's own gate.
translations.idiomatic: Raiding works because camps lie near the frontier—we strike unawares, withdraw quickly, and a step south brings us home.

sentences.zh: 復套，則深入其地，後援不繼，事勢異也。

translations.literal: Recovering the Ordos means penetrating deep into their territory with no follow-on support—the situation is entirely different.
translations.idiomatic: Recovering the Ordos means marching deep with no reliable support—the strategic situation is wholly different.

sentences.zh: 往城諸邊，近我土，彼原不以為利。

translations.literal: When we built forts along the frontier before, they were close to our soil, and the enemy originally did not regard them as valuable.
translations.idiomatic: Forts built along the frontier stood on our own ground—the enemy never considered them worth fighting for.

sentences.zh: 套，自其四時駐牧地，肯晏然已乎？

translations.literal: The Ordos is their pastureland for all four seasons—would they quietly acquiesce?
translations.idiomatic: The Ordos is their year-round pasture—would they passively surrender it?

sentences.zh: 事體異也。

translations.literal: The nature of the matter is different.
translations.idiomatic: The circumstances are entirely different.

sentences.zh: 曰伺彼出套，據河守，先亟築渡口垣墻，以次移置邊堡。

translations.literal: Some say: wait until they leave the Ordos, hold at the river, first urgently build walls at the crossings, then in sequence relocate frontier forts.
translations.idiomatic: Some propose waiting until they leave the Ordos, holding the river, urgently building walls at the crossings, then moving frontier forts forward step by step.

sentences.zh: 彼控弦十余萬，豈有空套出。

translations.literal: They have more than a hundred thousand bowmen—how could the Ordos ever be empty for them to leave?
translations.idiomatic: With more than a hundred thousand warriors under arms, how could the Ordos ever stand empty?

sentences.zh: 築垣二千餘里，豈不日可成？

translations.literal: Building walls more than two thousand li long—could that be finished in a day?
translations.idiomatic: Walls stretching two thousand li and more—could they be built in a day?

sentences.zh: 堡非百數十不相聯絡，堡兵非千人不可居，而遊僥瞭望者不與，當三十萬眾不止也。

translations.literal: Forts cannot link up unless there are scores of them; fort garrisons cannot be held with fewer than a thousand men each, and patrol and lookout troops are not counted—the force required would exceed three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Forts must number in the dozens to link together; each needs a garrison of at least a thousand, patrol troops not included—the total would exceed three hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 況循邊距河，動輒千里，一歲食糜億萬。

translations.literal: Moreover, following the frontier along the river for often a thousand li, a year's grain expenditure would run to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier runs along the river for a thousand li and more—a single year's rations would cost hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 自內輸邊，自邊輸河，飛挽之艱不可不深慮。

translations.literal: Transport from the interior to the frontier, from the frontier to the river—the difficulty of urgent grain convoys must be deeply considered.
translations.idiomatic: Grain must flow from the interior to the frontier, then from the frontier to the river—the strain of emergency convoys cannot be underestimated.

sentences.zh: 若令彼有其隙，我乘其敝，從而圖之，未嘗不可。

translations.literal: If we wait until they expose a gap and we seize their weakness to act accordingly, it is not impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until they expose a weakness, strike when they falter—then success is possible.

sentences.zh: 今塞下喘息未定，邊卒瘡痍未起，橫挑強寇以事非常，愚所不解也。

translations.literal: Now the frontier has barely caught its breath; the border troops' wounds have not yet healed—to defiantly provoke a powerful enemy over an extraordinary venture is what I cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier has barely recovered; border troops still bear their wounds. To deliberately provoke a powerful enemy on so rash a venture—I cannot comprehend it.

sentences.zh: 議上，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial went up; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne and was ignored.

sentences.zh: 其後，俺答與小王子隙。

translations.literal: Afterward Altan and the Little Prince had a falling-out.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Altan Khan and the Little Prince fell out.

sentences.zh: 小王子欲寇遼東，俺答以其謀告，請與中國夾攻以立信。

translations.literal: The Little Prince wished to raid Liaodong; Altan reported his plan and asked to join China in a pincer attack to establish good faith.
translations.idiomatic: When the Little Prince planned to raid Liaodong, Altan revealed the scheme and proposed a joint attack with Ming forces to prove his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 萬達不敢聞。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda did not dare to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda did not dare report this.

sentences.zh: 使者再至，為言於朝，帝不許。

translations.literal: When the envoys came again he spoke of it at court; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys arrived again Weng reported to court; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 二十七年三月，萬達又言諸部求貢不遂，慚且憤，聲言大舉犯邊，乞令邊臣得便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-seventh year Weng Wanda again reported that the various tribes, having failed to obtain tribute, were ashamed and enraged, proclaiming a great raid on the frontier, and asked that frontier officials be allowed discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 27 Weng reported that the tribes, rebuffed in their tribute requests, were shamed and furious, threatening massive raids, and asked that frontier officials be granted discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，切責之，通貢議乃絕。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, severely reproached him, and the talks on tribute were thus ended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, sharply rebuked him, and the entire tribute negotiation collapsed.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，俺答犯大同不克，退攻五堡，官軍戰彌陀山卻之。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month Altan attacked Datong without success, withdrew to attack the Five Forts, and government troops repelled him at battle on Mount Mituo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year Altan struck at Datong without success, then turned to attack the Five Forts, where government forces repelled him at Mount Mituo.

sentences.zh: 趨山西，復敗還。

translations.literal: He pressed toward Shanxi, was again defeated, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He drove toward Shanxi, was beaten again, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 逾月，犯宣府，大掠永寧、隆慶、懷來，軍民死者數萬。

translations.literal: After more than a month he raided Xuanfu, plundered Yongning, Longqing, and Huailai on a great scale, and tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians died.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he struck Xuanfu, ravaging Yongning, Longqing, and Huailai—tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians perished.

sentences.zh: 萬達坐停俸二級。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda was penalized by suspension of salary for two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda was penalized with a two-rank salary cut.

sentences.zh: 俄錄彌陀山功，還其俸。

translations.literal: Soon the Mount Mituo merit was recorded and his salary was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the victory at Mount Mituo was recognized and his salary restored.

sentences.zh: 俺答將復寇宣府，總兵官趙卿怯，萬達奏以周尚文代。

translations.literal: When Altan was about to raid Xuanfu again, regional commander Zhao Qing was timid, and Weng Wanda memorialized to replace him with Zhou Shangwen.
translations.idiomatic: As Altan prepared another strike on Xuanfu, regional commander Zhao Qing proved timid, and Weng memorialized to replace him with Zhou Shangwen.

sentences.zh: 未至，寇犯滴水崖，指揮董抃、江瀚、唐臣、張淮等戰死，遂南下駐隆慶石河營，分遊騎東掠。

translations.literal: Before Zhou arrived the raiders attacked Dishui Cliff; commanders Dong Bian, Jiang Han, Tang Chen, Zhang Huai, and others died in battle; then they went south and encamped at Shihé Camp in Longqing, sending out raiding cavalry eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhou arrived the raiders struck Dishui Cliff; commanders Dong Bian, Jiang Han, Tang Chen, and Zhang Huai fell in battle. The enemy then moved south to encamp at Shihé in Longqing and sent raiding parties east.

sentences.zh: 遊擊王鑰、大同遊擊袁正卻之，寇移而南。

translations.literal: Mobile-detachment commander Wang Yao and Datong mobile-detachment commander Yuan Zheng repelled them, and the raiders shifted southward.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile-detachment commanders Wang Yao and Yuan Zheng of Datong drove them back, and the raiders turned south.

sentences.zh: 會尚文萬騎至，參將田琦騎千余與合，連戰曹家莊、斬四首，搴其旗，寇據險不退。

translations.literal: When Shangwen arrived with ten thousand horsemen, vice commander Tian Qi with more than a thousand horsemen joined him; they fought continuously at Caojia Village, beheaded four, seized their banner, but the raiders held the high ground and would not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shangwen arrived with ten thousand horsemen; vice commander Tian Qi joined with a thousand cavalry. They fought at Caojia Village, took four heads and captured an enemy banner, but the raiders held the high ground and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 萬達督參將姜應熊等馳赴，順風鼓噪，揚沙蔽天。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda personally supervised vice commanders Jiang Yingxiong and others galloping to the scene; with the wind at their backs they beat drums and shouted, raising dust that blotted out the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda raced to the field with vice commander Jiang Yingxiong and others; with the wind at their backs they raised a thunderous clamor, dust swirling until it blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 寇驚曰：「翁太師至矣！

translations.literal: The raiders cried in alarm: "Grand Mentor Weng has arrived!
translations.idiomatic: The raiders shouted in alarm: "Grand Mentor Weng is here!

sentences.zh: 」是夜東去。

translations.literal: " That night they departed eastward.
translations.idiomatic: " That night they withdrew eastward.

sentences.zh: 諸將追擊，連敗之。

translations.literal: The generals pursued and defeated them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The generals pursued and routed them repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 帝偵萬達督戰狀，大喜，立進兵部尚書兼右副都御史。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of Weng Wanda's conduct in directing the battle, was greatly pleased, and immediately promoted him to Minister of War and Concurrent Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Learning how Weng commanded the battle, the emperor was delighted and immediately promoted him to Minister of War with concurrent appointment as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尋召理部事。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to administer the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to head the ministry.

sentences.zh: 以父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，大同失事，督撫郭宗臯、陳耀被逮，詔起萬達代宗臯。

translations.literal: The next autumn Datong suffered a disaster; grand coordinators Guo Zonggao and Chen Yao were arrested, and an edict recalled Weng Wanda to replace Zonggao.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn disaster struck Datong; grand coordinators Guo Zonggao and Chen Yao were arrested, and Weng was recalled by edict to replace Guo.

sentences.zh: 萬達方病疽，廬墓間，疏請終制。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda was then suffering from an abscess and was living by his father's tomb; he memorialized asking to complete the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Weng was then ill with an abscess and living by his father's grave; he memorialized to complete his mourning obligations.

sentences.zh: 未達，而俺答犯都城。

translations.literal: Before the memorial arrived Altan raided the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Before his memorial reached court, Altan struck at the capital.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書丁汝夔得罪，遂即以萬達代之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Ding Ruai incurred disgrace, and Weng Wanda was immediately appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Ding Ruai fell from favor, and Weng was appointed in his stead.

sentences.zh: 萬達家嶺南，距京師八千里，倍道行四十日抵近京。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda's family was in Lingnan, eight thousand li from the capital; traveling by forced marches he reached the vicinity of the capital in forty days.
translations.idiomatic: Weng's home was in Lingnan, eight thousand li from the capital; he traveled by forced marches and reached the outskirts of Beijing in forty days.

sentences.zh: 時寇氛熾，帝日夕徯萬達至。

translations.literal: At the time the threat of raiders was blazing; the emperor awaited Weng Wanda's arrival day and night.
translations.idiomatic: With the raider threat at its height, the emperor waited day and night for Weng's arrival.

sentences.zh: 遲之，以問嚴嵩。

translations.literal: When he was delayed, the emperor asked Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Weng was slow to arrive, the emperor turned to Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩故不悅萬達，言寇患在肘腋，諸臣觀望，非君召不俟駕之義。

translations.literal: Yan Song had never liked Weng Wanda; he said the raider threat was at the emperor's very elbow, the officials were watching and waiting, and this was not the righteousness of answering the sovereign's summons without waiting for the carriage to be ready.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song, who had always disliked Weng, said the enemy was at the emperor's very gates while officials dallied—hardly the loyalty owed a sovereign's urgent summons.

sentences.zh: 帝遂用王邦瑞於兵部。

translations.literal: The emperor then appointed Wang Bangrui to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accordingly appointed Wang Bangrui as Minister of War instead.

sentences.zh: 不數日，萬達至，具疏自明。

translations.literal: Within a few days Weng Wanda arrived and submitted a detailed memorial clearing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Weng arrived and submitted a detailed memorial in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 帝責其欺慢，念守制，姑奪職，聽別用。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for disrespect, but mindful that he was in mourning, merely stripped his office for the time being and allowed appointment elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for insolence but, considering his mourning obligations, stripped his rank for the moment and permitted other appointment.

sentences.zh: 仇鸞時為大將軍，寵方盛，銜宿怨，讒言構於帝。

translations.literal: At the time Qiu Luan was grand general and was at the height of favor; nursing an old grudge, he slandered Weng before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Luan, then grand general and at the height of imperial favor, nursed an old grudge and poisoned the emperor against Weng with slander.

sentences.zh: 萬達遂失眷，降兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，經略紫荊諸關。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda thus lost favor, was demoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of War and Concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, and was assigned to command the Zijing Pass and related gates.
translations.idiomatic: Weng lost imperial favor, was demoted to Vice Minister of War with concurrent appointment as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, and assigned to oversee the Zijing and related passes.

sentences.zh: 三十年二月，京察，自陳乞終制。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirtieth year, during the capital evaluation of officials, he volunteered a request to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 30, at the capital personnel review, he asked to be allowed to complete his mourning.

sentences.zh: 帝疑其避事，免歸。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected he was shirking duty and dismissed him to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected he was evading duty and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 瀕行疏謝，復摘訛字為不敬，斥為民。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he submitted a farewell memorial; the emperor again picked out textual errors as disrespect and banished him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his departure he submitted a farewell memorial; the emperor seized on textual errors as disrespect and stripped him of all rank.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，兵部尚書趙錦以附仇鸞戍邊，復起萬達代之。

translations.literal: The next year in the tenth month Minister of War Zhao Jin was banished to the frontier for siding with Qiu Luan, and Weng Wanda was again raised to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The following tenth month, Minister Zhao Jin was exiled to the frontier for aligning with Qiu Luan, and Weng was recalled to replace him.

sentences.zh: 未聞命卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: Before he received the appointment he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died before the edict reached him, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 萬達事親孝。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda was filial in serving his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda was devoted filially to his parents.

sentences.zh: 父歿，負土成墳。

translations.literal: When his father died he carried earth to build the tomb mound himself.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he personally carried earth to build the tomb mound.

sentences.zh: 好談性命之學，與歐陽德、羅洪先、唐順之、王畿、魏良政善。

translations.literal: He loved to discuss learning on nature and destiny and was on good terms with Ouyang De, Luo Hongxian, Tang Shunzhi, Wang Ji, and Wei Liangzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in philosophical discourse and was close to Ouyang De, Luo Hongxian, Tang Shunzhi, Wang Ji, and Wei Liangzheng.

sentences.zh: 通古今，操筆頃刻萬言。

translations.literal: He was versed in antiquity and the present and could wield the brush to produce ten thousand words in a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite in history and the present, he could write ten thousand words in a sitting.

sentences.zh: 為人剛介坦直，勇於任事，履艱危，意氣彌厲。

translations.literal: As a man he was stern, upright, and frank; bold in undertaking affairs; when facing danger his spirit grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: Stern, upright, and plain-spoken, he was bold in action; the graver the danger, the fiercer his resolve.

sentences.zh: 臨陣嘗身先士卒，尤善禦將士，得其死力。

translations.literal: In battle he often led from the front; he was especially skilled at commanding troops and winning their utmost loyalty unto death.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he led from the front; he excelled at commanding men and winning their utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，邊臣行事適機宜、建言中肯窾者，萬達稱首。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era, among frontier officials whose actions suited the moment and whose memorialized advice hit the vital point, Weng Wanda ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Among Jiajing frontier officials whose actions matched circumstances and whose counsel hit the mark, Weng Wanda stood first.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，追謚襄毅。

translations.literal: In the Longqing era he was posthumously given the title Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Longqing reign he was posthumously honored with the title Xiangyi (Resolute and Fierce).

sentences.zh: 贊曰：楊一清、王瓊俱負才略，著績邊陲，有人倫鑒，鋤奸定難因以成功。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yang Yiqing and Wang Qiong both possessed talent and strategy, achieved distinction on the frontier, had discernment in human relations, and succeeded by rooting out traitors and settling crises.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Yang Yiqing and Wang Qiong both possessed talent and strategic vision, distinguished themselves on the frontier, showed keen judgment of character, and succeeded by rooting out traitors and quelling crises.

sentences.zh: 亦俱任智數。

translations.literal: Both also relied on cunning stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Both also relied on clever stratagem.

sentences.zh: 然瓊，其權譎之尤歟！

translations.literal: Yet as for Wang Qiong—is he not the most extreme in resourceful scheming!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Qiong was surely the most consummate master of cunning intrigue!

sentences.zh: 彭澤望甚偉，顧處置哈密，抑何舛也。

translations.literal: Peng Ze's bearing was very imposing, yet in handling Hami—how mistaken!
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze cut an imposing figure, yet his handling of Hami—how badly misjudged!

sentences.zh: 毛伯溫能任翁萬達、張嶽，以成安南之功，不失為持重將。

translations.literal: Mao Bowen was able to employ Weng Wanda and Zhang Yue to accomplish the achievement in Annam; he may still be counted a weighty, steady commander.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bowen knew how to deploy Weng Wanda and Zhang Yue to win the Annam campaign—a commander's measured judgment, at least.

sentences.zh: 萬達飭邊備，整軍實，其爭復套，知彼知己，尤深識遠慮雲。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda disciplined frontier defenses and consolidated military strength; in his debate over recovering the Ordos, knowing both friend and foe, he showed especially deep insight and far-sighted planning.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda strengthened frontier defenses and rebuilt military capacity; in his opposition to recovering the Ordos he knew both enemy and self, and displayed especially penetrating insight and long vision.
